title.zh: 卷一百五十四 列傳第七十九 李晟子:愿 憲 愬 聽
title.en: Volume 154 Biographies 79: Li Cheng and sons: Yuan, Xian, Su, Ting
title.raw: 卷一百五十四 列傳第七十九 李晟子:愿 憲 愬 聽 Volume 154 Biographies 79: Li Cheng and sons: Yuan, Xian, Su, Ting

sentences.zh: 李晟子:愿 憲 愬 聽 聽子:琢 甥:王佖

translations.literal: Li Sheng's sons: Yuan, Xian, Su, Ting; Su's son: Zhuo; nephew: Wang Tian
translations.idiomatic: Sons of Li Sheng: Yuan, Xian, Su, and Ting; Su's son: Zhuo; nephew: Wang Tian

sentences.zh: 李晟，字良器，洮州臨潭人。

translations.literal: Li Sheng, styled Liangqi, was a man of Lintan in Taozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng, courtesy name Liangqi, was a native of Lintan in Taozhou.

sentences.zh: 世以武力仕，然位不過裨將。

translations.literal: For generations they served through martial prowess, yet rank never exceeded deputy general.
translations.idiomatic: His family had served by force of arms for generations, yet none had risen higher than deputy general.

sentences.zh: 晟幼孤，奉母孝。

translations.literal: Sheng was orphaned young and served his mother with filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng lost his father in childhood and devoted himself to his mother with exemplary filial care.

sentences.zh: 身長六尺。

translations.literal: His body was six chi in height.
translations.idiomatic: He stood six chi tall.

sentences.zh: 年十八，往事河西王忠嗣，從擊吐蕃。

translations.literal: At age eighteen he went to serve Heyi Wang Zhongsi and followed in attacking the Tibetans.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he entered the service of Wang Zhongsi, Prince of Heyi, and campaigned against the Tibetans.

sentences.zh: 悍酋乘城，殺傷士甚眾，忠嗣怒，募射者，晟挾一矢殪之，三軍歡奮。

translations.literal: A fierce chieftain mounted the wall and killed and wounded very many soldiers; Zhongsi in anger recruited archers; Sheng with one arrow brought him down, and the three armies rejoiced and were stirred.
translations.idiomatic: A fierce enemy leader manned the walls and inflicted heavy casualties; Zhongsi, enraged, called for archers, and Sheng felled him with a single arrow, whereupon the whole army erupted in cheers.

sentences.zh: 忠嗣撫其背曰：「萬人敵也。」

translations.literal: Zhongsi stroked his back and said, "A match for ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongsi clapped him on the back and said, "Here is a man who could face ten thousand alone.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔節度使高升召署列將，擊疊州叛羌于高當川，又擊連狂羌於罕山，破之。

translations.literal: The Fengxiang military commissioner Gao Sheng summoned and appointed him a ranked commander; he attacked rebellious Qiang of Diezhou at Gaodang River and again attacked the Lian-Kuang Qiang at Hanshan, defeating them.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Sheng, military commissioner of Fengxiang, summoned him and made him a ranked commander; he struck the rebel Qiang of Diezhou at Gaodang River and again routed the Lian-Kuang Qiang at Hanshan.

sentences.zh: 累遷左羽林大將軍。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to General of the Left Inspired Awesomeness Army.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through repeated promotions to General of the Left Inspired Awesomeness Army.

sentences.zh: 廣德初，擊党項有功，授特進，試太常卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Guangde era, in attacking the Tangut he had merit and was granted Special Advancement and provisional appointment as Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Guangde reign he distinguished himself fighting the Tangut and was granted the honorary title Special Advancement with provisional appointment as Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 大曆初，李抱玉署晟右軍將。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Dali era, Li Baoyu appointed Sheng Right Army General.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dali reign Li Baoyu appointed Sheng general of the right army.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃寇靈州，抱玉授以兵五千擊之，辭曰：「以眾則不足，以謀則多。」

translations.literal: The Tibetans raided Lingzhou; Baoyu gave him five thousand troops to strike them; he declined, saying, "For numbers they are insufficient; for stratagem they are too many.
translations.idiomatic: When Tibetans threatened Lingzhou, Baoyu gave him five thousand men to repel them; he declined, saying, "For a frontal fight that is too few; for a stratagem it is too many.

sentences.zh: 乃請千人。

translations.literal: He then requested one thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: He asked instead for a thousand men.

sentences.zh: 由大震關趨臨洮，屠定秦堡，執其帥慕容谷鐘，虜乃解靈州去。

translations.literal: By way of Dazhen Pass he hastened to Lintao, slaughtered Dingqin Fort, seized its commander Murong Guzhong, and the barbarians then lifted the siege of Lingzhou and departed.
translations.idiomatic: He marched through Dazhen Pass toward Lintao, stormed Dingqin Fort, captured its commander Murong Guzhong, and the invaders thereupon abandoned their siege of Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 遷開府儀同三司，以右金吾衛大將軍為涇原、四鎮、北庭兵馬使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Preceptor of the Palace with the same ceremonial rank as the Three Excellencies, and as General of the Right Golden Crow Guard became military commissioner of Jingyuan, the Four Garrisons, and Beiting.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Preceptor with ceremonial parity to the Three Excellencies and, while serving as General of the Right Golden Crow Guard, was made overseer of troops for Jingyuan, the Four Garrisons, and Beiting.

sentences.zh: 馬璘與吐蕃戰鹽倉，敗績；

translations.literal: Ma Lin fought the Tibetans at Yancang and was defeated;
translations.idiomatic: Ma Lin was defeated by the Tibetans at Yancang;

sentences.zh: 晟率遊兵拔璘以歸，封合川郡王。

translations.literal: Sheng led light troops to rescue Lin and bring him back, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Hechuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng led a flying column to extricate Lin and escort him to safety, for which he was enfeoffed as Prince of Hechuan.

sentences.zh: 璘內忌晟威略，歸之朝，為右神策都將。

translations.literal: Lin inwardly resented Sheng's martial renown and sent him back to court, where he became chief commander of the Right Divine Strategy Army.
translations.idiomatic: Lin, jealous of Sheng's reputation and ability, recalled him to the capital, where he was made chief commander of the Right Divine Strategy Army.

sentences.zh: 德宗始立，吐蕃寇劍南，方崔寧未還，蜀土大震，詔晟將神策兵救之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Dezong had just ascended, the Tibetans raided Jiannan; Cui Ning had not yet returned, and the land of Shu was greatly shaken; an edict ordered Sheng to lead Divine Strategy troops to rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after Emperor Dezong took the throne, Tibetans invaded Jiannan while Cui Ning was still absent; panic swept Shu, and the emperor ordered Sheng to lead the Divine Strategy Army to the relief of the region.

sentences.zh: 逾漏天，拔飛越等三城，絕大渡，斬虜千級，虜遁去。

translations.literal: He crossed Leak-Heaven Pass, captured Feiyue and two other cities, severed the Great Crossing, beheaded the enemy by the thousands, and the barbarians fled away.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the treacherous Leak-Heaven Pass, took Feiyue and two other strongholds, cut the enemy off at the Dadu River, killed thousands, and drove the invaders into flight.

sentences.zh: 建中二年，魏博田悅反，晟為神策先鋒，與河東馬燧、昭義李抱真合兵攻之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianzhong, Tian Yue of Weibo rebelled; Sheng was vanguard of the Divine Strategy Army and joined forces with Ma Sui of Hedong and Li Baozhen of Zhaoyi to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianzhong year 2, Tian Yue of Weibo rose in rebellion; Sheng served as vanguard of the Divine Strategy Army and marched with Ma Sui of Hedong and Li Baozhen of Zhaoyi against him.

sentences.zh: 斬楊朝光，晟乘冰度洺水，破悅；

translations.literal: Yang Chaoguang was beheaded; Sheng crossed the Ming River on the ice and defeated Yue;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Chaoguang was executed; Sheng crossed the frozen Ming River and routed Yue;

sentences.zh: 又戰洹水，悅大敗，遂進攻魏。

translations.literal: Again they fought at the Huan River; Yue was greatly defeated, and they then advanced to attack Wei.
translations.idiomatic: At another battle on the Huan River Yue suffered a crushing defeat, and the allies pressed on toward Wei.

sentences.zh: 加檢校左散騎常侍，兼魏府左司馬。

translations.literal: He was given the additional title of Acting Left Regular Attendant and concurrently made Left Staff Major of the Wei prefectural headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He received the additional post of Acting Left Regular Attendant and was made left staff major at the Wei headquarters.

sentences.zh: 硃滔、王武俊圍康日知于趙州也，抱真分兵二千戍邢，燧怒，欲班師。

translations.literal: Zhu Tao and Wang Wujun were besieging Kang Rizhi at Zhaozhou; Baozhen detached two thousand men to garrison Xing; Sui grew angry and wished to withdraw his army.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhu Tao and Wang Wujun besieged Kang Rizhi at Zhaozhou, Baozhen posted two thousand men to garrison Xing; Sui, furious, threatened to pull his forces out.

sentences.zh: 晟曰：「奉詔東討者，吾三帥也。

translations.literal: Sheng said, "Those who received the edict to campaign east are we three commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng said, "The three of us were the ones ordered east to suppress the rebels.

sentences.zh: 邢、趙比壤，今賊以兵加趙，是邢有晝夜憂，李公分眾守之，不為過，公奈何遽引去！」

translations.literal: Xing and Zhao are neighboring soil; now the rebels press Zhao with troops, so Xing has worry day and night; for Lord Li to divide forces to guard it is no excess—why should you, sir, hastily withdraw!
translations.idiomatic: Xing and Zhao lie side by side; with the enemy hammering Zhao, Xing lives under constant threat. For Lord Li to detach troops to hold Xing is no fault—why would you, sir, march away so soon!

sentences.zh: 燧悟，釋然，即造抱真壘，與交歡。

translations.literal: Sui understood, was relieved, and at once went to Baozhen's camp and renewed friendly relations.
translations.idiomatic: Sui took the point, his anger subsided, and he went straight to Baozhen's camp to restore amity between them.

sentences.zh: 晟建言：「以兵趨定州，與張孝忠合，以圖范陽，則武俊等當舍趙。」

translations.literal: Sheng proposed: "Take troops toward Dingzhou, join Zhang Xiaozhong, and aim at Fanyang—then Wujun and the rest should abandon Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng urged, "March on Dingzhou, unite with Zhang Xiaozhong, and strike at Fanyang—the rebels at Zhao will have to lift their siege.

sentences.zh: 帝壯之，授御史大夫，又俾神策三將軍莫仁擢等隸之。

translations.literal: The emperor was impressed and appointed him Censor-in-Chief, and also placed under him the three Divine Strategy generals Mo Renzhuo and others.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the plan, made him Censor-in-Chief, and placed the three Divine Strategy generals Mo Renzhuo and others under his command.

sentences.zh: 晟自魏引而北，武俊果解去。

translations.literal: Sheng led his forces north from Wei, and Wujun indeed lifted the siege and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng marched north from Wei, and Wujun, as predicted, broke off the siege and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 晟留趙三日，與孝忠連兵，北略恒州。

translations.literal: Sheng remained at Zhao three days, joined arms with Xiaozhong, and raided north toward Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After three days at Zhao he joined Xiaozhong and swept north toward Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 圍硃滔將鄭景濟于清苑，決水灌之。

translations.literal: He besieged Zhu Tao's general Zheng Jingji at Qingyuan and breached the dikes to flood them.
translations.idiomatic: He invested Zhu Tao's general Zheng Jingji at Qingyuan and broke the dikes to flood the town.

sentences.zh: 悅、武俊引兵戰白樓，孝忠兵笮，晟引步騎擊破之，清苑益急。

translations.literal: Yue and Wujun led troops to fight at Bailou; Xiaozhong's army was cramped; Sheng led infantry and cavalry to defeat them, and the plight at Qingyuan grew more pressing.
translations.idiomatic: Yue and Wujun gave battle at Bailou; with Xiaozhong's forces pinned, Sheng led foot and horse to break them, tightening the noose on Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 滔、武俊大懼，悉起兵來救，圍晟軍。

translations.literal: Tao and Wujun were greatly afraid and mustered all their forces to rescue, surrounding Sheng's army.
translations.idiomatic: Tao and Wujun, in alarm, raised their full strength to relieve the siege and encircled Sheng's army.

sentences.zh: 晟內攻景濟而外抗滔等，自正月至五月不解。

translations.literal: Sheng pressed Jingji within while resisting Tao and the rest without, from the first month to the fifth month without respite.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng hammered Jingji from within while holding Tao and the others at bay without, and from the first month to the fifth the fighting never let up.

sentences.zh: 會晟疾甚，不能興，軍中共計引還定州，而賊猶不敢逼。

translations.literal: When Sheng's illness grew severe and he could not rise, the army jointly planned to withdraw to Dingzhou, yet the rebels still did not dare press them.
translations.idiomatic: When Sheng fell gravely ill and could not leave his bed, the army resolved to fall back on Dingzhou—and even then the enemy did not dare close in.

sentences.zh: 疾間，將復進，會帝出奉天，有詔召晟即日治嚴。

translations.literal: In a remission of the illness he was about to advance again when the emperor departed for Fengtian; an edict summoned Sheng to prepare to march that very day.
translations.idiomatic: As he recovered and prepared to advance again, the emperor fled to Fengtian; an edict ordered Sheng to strike camp and march at once.

sentences.zh: 而孝忠以軍介二盜間，倚晟為重，數止晟無西。

translations.literal: But Xiaozhong, with his army caught between two rebel bands, relied on Sheng as his mainstay and repeatedly urged Sheng not to go west.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhong, his army wedged between two rebel hosts, depended on Sheng as his anchor and repeatedly begged him not to march west.

sentences.zh: 晟語眾曰：「天子播越，人臣當百舍一息。

translations.literal: Sheng told the assembly, "The Son of Heaven is cast adrift; as subjects we should travel a hundred lodges with one breath.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng told his men, "The emperor is in exile; a loyal subject should not spare himself even if he must march a hundred stages without rest.

sentences.zh: 義武欲止吾，吾當以子為質。」

translations.literal: Yiwu wishes to stop me—I shall leave my son as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: If Yiwu tries to hold me back, I will leave my son with him as pledge.

sentences.zh: 乃以憑約昏，並遺良馬。

translations.literal: He then pledged a marriage alliance and also sent fine horses.
translations.idiomatic: He sealed the bond with a marriage alliance and sent fine horses as well.

sentences.zh: 孝忠有親將謁晟，晟解玉帶遺之，使喻孝忠。

translations.literal: Xiaozhong had a close officer visit Sheng; Sheng removed his jade belt and gave it to him, bidding him explain to Xiaozhong.
translations.idiomatic: When one of Xiaozhong's trusted officers came to see him, Sheng took off his jade belt and sent it back with a message for Xiaozhong.

sentences.zh: 乃得逾飛孤，次代州，詔迎拜神策行營節度使。

translations.literal: Only then could he cross Feigu Pass, halt at Daizhou, and by edict was welcomed and appointed military commissioner of the Divine Strategy campaigning army.
translations.idiomatic: Thus he crossed Feigu Pass and halted at Daizhou, where an edict received him and named him military commissioner of the Divine Strategy field army.

sentences.zh: 進臨渭北，壁東渭橋，所過樵蘇無犯。

translations.literal: He advanced to the north bank of the Wei, encamped at East Wei Bridge, and along the route did not violate firewood or forage.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed to the north bank of the Wei, fortified East Wei Bridge, and forbade his men to touch so much as a stick of firewood along the march.

sentences.zh: 時劉德信自扈澗敗歸，亦次渭南，軍囂無制。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Dexin, returning defeated from Hujian, also halted at Weinan; his army was unruly and undisciplined.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Dexin, beaten back from Hujian, was also camped at Weinan with a disorderly, undisciplined force.

sentences.zh: 德信入謁晟，晟責所以敗，斬之，以數騎入壁勞其軍，無敢動。

translations.literal: Dexin entered to pay respects to Sheng; Sheng reproached him for the defeat and beheaded him, then with a few horsemen entered the camp to comfort his army, and none dared stir.
translations.idiomatic: When Dexin came to pay his respects, Sheng held him to account for the defeat and executed him, then rode into the camp with a handful of men to reassure the troops—and not a man stirred.

sentences.zh: 晟已並兵，則軍益振。

translations.literal: Once Sheng had merged the armies, the force grew still more vigorous.
translations.idiomatic: With both armies under his command, morale surged.

sentences.zh: 於是朔方李懷光方軍咸陽，不欲晟當一面，請與晟合。

translations.literal: Then Li Huai'guang of Shuofang was encamped at Xianyang and did not wish Sheng to hold a separate front; he requested to unite with Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huai'guang of Shuofang was then at Xianyang and, unwilling to let Sheng hold an independent command, asked to combine their forces.

sentences.zh: 有詔徙屯，乃引趨陳濤斜，與懷光聯壘。

translations.literal: An edict ordered relocation of the camp; he then led his troops toward Chantaoxie and joined camps with Huai'guang.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order he moved camp, marched to Chantaoxie, and pitched beside Huai'guang.

sentences.zh: 晟每與賊戰，必錦裘繡帽自表，指顧陣前。

translations.literal: Whenever Sheng fought the rebels he always displayed himself in brocade robe and embroidered cap, directing and surveying before the battle line.
translations.idiomatic: In every battle with the rebels Sheng appeared in brocade and an embroidered cap, directing affairs in plain sight before the ranks.

sentences.zh: 懷光望見，惡之，戒曰：「將務持重，豈宜自表襮，為賊餌哉！」

translations.literal: Huai'guang saw this and disliked it, admonishing him: "A general must keep weight and steadiness—how can you display yourself so conspicuously and become bait for the enemy!
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang saw it and took offense, warning him, "A commander must keep his gravity—why show yourself so boldly and offer the enemy a target!

sentences.zh: 晟曰：「昔在涇原，士頗相畏伏，欲令見之，奪其心爾。」

translations.literal: Sheng said, "Formerly in Jingyuan the soldiers were quite in awe; I wish them to see me and seize their hearts—that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Sheng replied, "Back in Jingyuan the men knew me and feared me; I want them to see me again and break the enemy's spirit—that is all."

sentences.zh: 懷光不悅，遷延有異志。

translations.literal: Huai'guang was displeased, delayed action, and harbored divergent intentions.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang grew resentful, dragged his feet, and began to nurse rebellious designs.

sentences.zh: 晟使間說懷光曰：「賊據京邑，天子暴露于外，公宜速進兵。

translations.literal: Sheng sent an intermediary to persuade Huai'guang, saying, "The rebels hold the capital; the Son of Heaven is exposed outside—you, sir, ought to advance troops quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng sent an emissary to urge Huai'guang: "The rebels hold the capital while the emperor suffers in the open—you should strike at once.

sentences.zh: 雖晟不肖，願為公先驅，死且不悔。」

translations.literal: Though Sheng is unworthy, I am willing to be your vanguard—even in death I shall not regret it.
translations.idiomatic: Unworthy as I am, I will lead the van for you and die without regret.

sentences.zh: 懷光不納。

translations.literal: Huai'guang did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang would not listen.

sentences.zh: 每兵至都城下，而懷光軍多鹵掠，晟軍整戢。

translations.literal: Whenever troops reached below the capital, Huai'guang's army mostly plundered, while Sheng's army was orderly and restrained.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever they drew near the capital, Huai'guang's men looted freely while Sheng's held strict discipline.

sentences.zh: 懷光使分所獲遺之，又辭不敢受。

translations.literal: Huai'guang sent a share of the booty to him, but he again declined, not daring to accept.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang tried to share the spoils with him, but Sheng refused each gift.

sentences.zh: 懷光謀沮撓其軍，即奏言：「神策兵給賜比方鎮獨厚，今桀逆未平，軍不可以異。

translations.literal: Huai'guang plotted to thwart and shake his army and memorialized, saying, "Divine Strategy troops receive rations and gifts thicker than the border commands alone; now the fierce rebels are not yet pacified—the armies must not be treated differently.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking to undermine Sheng's troops, Huai'guang memorialized that the Divine Strategy Army was paid more lavishly than the frontier commands and that, with rebellion still raging, such inequality could not stand.

sentences.zh: 且眾以為言，臣無以解。

translations.literal: Moreover the masses speak of it, and your servant has no way to explain it away.
translations.idiomatic: My own men are complaining, and I have no answer for them.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下裁處。」

translations.literal: May Your Majesty alone decide.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to decide.

sentences.zh: 懷光欲晟自削其軍，則士怨易撓。

translations.literal: Huai'guang wished Sheng himself to cut down his army, so that when the soldiers resented it they would be easy to shake.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang hoped Sheng would cut his own pay so that resentful troops would be easy to break.

sentences.zh: 帝議諸軍與神策等，力且不贍，遣翰林學士陸贄臨詔懷光，令與晟計所宜者。

translations.literal: The emperor considered equalizing all armies with the Divine Strategy and the like, but strength and resources would not suffice; he sent Hanlin academician Lu Zhi with the edict to Huai'guang, ordering him and Sheng to deliberate what was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: The court debated equalizing pay across the armies but lacked the means; the emperor sent Hanlin scholar Lu Zhi with the edict to Huai'guang, bidding him and Sheng work out a fair arrangement.

sentences.zh: 懷光曰：「稟賜不均，軍何以戰！」

translations.literal: Huai'guang said, "When rations and gifts are unequal, how can the army fight!
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang declared, "Unequal pay means an army that will not fight!

sentences.zh: 贄數顧晟，晟曰：「公，元帥，軍政得專之。

translations.literal: Zhi repeatedly looked toward Sheng; Sheng said, "You, sir, are the commander-in-chief—military affairs you may decide alone.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi glanced repeatedly at Sheng, who said, "You are supreme commander—military affairs are yours to decide.

sentences.zh: 晟將一軍，唯所命，其增損費調，敢不聽？」

translations.literal: Sheng commands one army and obeys only your orders; as to increasing or decreasing expenses and supplies, how would I dare not obey?
translations.idiomatic: I lead one army and obey you alone; raise or cut our allowances as you see fit—I will not object.

sentences.zh: 懷光默然計塞，顧刻削稟賜事出己，乃止。

translations.literal: Huai'guang fell silent, his stratagem blocked; seeing that cutting rations and gifts would come from himself, he then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang fell silent, his scheme collapsed: any cut would be his own doing, and he dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 懷光屯咸陽凡八旬，帝數促戰，以伺賊隙為言，卒不出兵，陰通硃泚，反跡浸露。

translations.literal: Huai'guang encamped at Xianyang for eighty days in all; the emperor repeatedly urged battle, but he spoke of watching for gaps in the rebels and in the end did not move troops; he secretly communicated with Zhu Ci, and signs of rebellion gradually appeared.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang lingered at Xianyang for eighty days; though the emperor repeatedly ordered him to fight, he pleaded the need to watch for an opening and never advanced, while secretly dealing with Zhu Ci until his treason could no longer be hidden.

sentences.zh: 晟懼為所並，上言：「當先變製備，請假裨佐趙光銑、唐良臣、張彧為洋、利、劍三州刺史，各勒兵以通蜀、漢衿喉。」

translations.literal: Sheng feared being absorbed by him and memorialized, "We should first change preparations; I request provisional appointment of my aides Zhao Guangxian, Tang Liangchen, and Zhang Yu as prefects of Yang, Li, and Jian, each leading troops to open the throat between Shu and Han.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing absorption by Huai'guang, Sheng urged preemptive redeployment: appoint his lieutenants Zhao Guangxian, Tang Liangchen, and Zhang Yu provisional governors of Yang, Li, and Jian, each with troops to secure the corridor between Shu and Han.

sentences.zh: 未報。

translations.literal: No reply came.
translations.idiomatic: The court never answered.

sentences.zh: 會吐蕃欲佐誅泚，帝議幸咸陽督戰，懷光大駭，疑帝奪其軍，圖反益急。

translations.literal: When the Tibetans wished to help execute Zhu Ci, the emperor considered visiting Xianyang to supervise the war; Huai'guang was greatly alarmed, suspected the emperor meant to seize his army, and plotted rebellion all the more urgently.
translations.idiomatic: When Tibet offered help against Zhu Ci, the emperor thought of going to Xianyang to direct operations; Huai'guang panicked, fearing the emperor meant to strip him of command, and hurried his rebellion forward.

sentences.zh: 晟與李建徽、陽惠元皆聯屯，適有使者到晟軍，晟乃令曰：「有詔徙屯。」

translations.literal: Sheng, Li Jianhui, and Yang Huiyuan were all encamped together; just then an envoy arrived at Sheng's army, and Sheng thereupon ordered, "There is an edict to relocate the camp.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng was encamped with Li Jianhui and Yang Huiyuan when an envoy reached his lines; Sheng immediately announced, "We have orders to move camp.

sentences.zh: 即結陣趨東渭橋。

translations.literal: At once he formed ranks and hastened to East Wei Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: He formed up at once and marched for East Wei Bridge.

sentences.zh: 後數日，懷光並建徽、惠元兵，惠元死之。

translations.literal: Several days later Huai'guang absorbed the armies of Jianhui and Huiyuan, and Huiyuan died in the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Days later Huai'guang seized the forces of Jianhui and Huiyuan; Huiyuan was killed in the struggle.

sentences.zh: 是日，帝進狩梁州，駱穀道隘，儲供不豫，從官乏食，帝歎曰：「早用晟言，三蜀之利，可坐有也。」

translations.literal: That day the emperor advanced in hunt to Liangzhou; the Luogu road was narrow, stores and supplies were not prepared, and the attendant officials lacked food; the emperor sighed, "Had we early used Sheng's counsel, the advantages of the Three Shu could have been had while sitting.
translations.idiomatic: That same day the emperor fled toward Liangzhou; the Luogu Pass was cramped, supplies had not been laid in, and his entourage went hungry. He sighed, "Had I heeded Sheng in time, the wealth of the Three Shu would already be ours.

sentences.zh: 顧渾瑊曰：「渭橋在賊腹中，兵孤絕，晟能辦勝邪？」

translations.literal: He turned to Hun Jian and said, "East Wei Bridge lies in the rebels' belly; the army is isolated—can Sheng achieve victory?"
translations.idiomatic: Turning to Hun Jian he asked, "East Wei Bridge sits deep in enemy country with a lone army—can Sheng possibly win?"

sentences.zh: 瑊曰：「晟秉義挺忠，崒然不可奪。

translations.literal: Jian said, "Sheng upholds righteousness and stands in loyalty; towering, he cannot be shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Jian answered, "Sheng is steadfast in loyalty and purpose—nothing will shake him.

sentences.zh: 臣策之，必破賊。」

translations.literal: Your servant calculates that he will surely break the rebels."
translations.idiomatic: I am certain he will crush the rebels."

sentences.zh: 帝乃安。

translations.literal: The emperor then was reassured.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took heart.

sentences.zh: 自行在遣晟將張少弘口詔進晟尚書左僕射、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: From the traveling court he sent Sheng's general Zhang Shaohong with an oral edict promoting Sheng to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Concurrent Grand Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: From the imperial refuge he sent Zhang Shaohong with an oral edict promoting Sheng to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 晟受命，拜且泣曰：「京師天下本，若皆執羈靮，誰將復之！」

translations.literal: Sheng received the appointment, bowed and wept, saying, "The capital is the root of the realm—if all hold the bridle, who will restore it!
translations.idiomatic: Accepting the commission, Sheng bowed and wept: "The capital is the heart of the empire—if every man holds back, who will win it back?

sentences.zh: 乃繕甲兵，治陴隍，以圖收復。

translations.literal: He then repaired armor and weapons, restored walls and moats, and planned recovery.
translations.idiomatic: He set about repairing arms and fortifications, preparing to retake the capital.

sentences.zh: 是時，晟提孤軍橫當寇鋒，恐二盜合以軋之，則卑詞厚幣，偽致誠於懷光者。

translations.literal: At this time Sheng led a lone army athwart the rebels' spearhead; fearing the two rebel hosts would unite to crush him, he used humble words and rich gifts, feigning sincerity toward Huai'guang.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng now held a lone army squarely in the enemy's path; lest Huai'guang and Zhu Ci unite against him, he flattered Huai'guang with humble words and lavish gifts, feigning loyalty.

sentences.zh: 時敖廥單覂，乃使張彧假京兆少尹，多署吏，調畿內賦，不淹旬，芻米告具。

translations.literal: At the time the granaries were empty and depleted; he made Zhang Yu acting Vice Magistrate of Jingzhao, appointed many clerks, and levied taxes within the capital region—in less than ten days fodder and grain were reported complete.
translations.idiomatic: With the granaries bare, he made Zhang Yu acting vice magistrate of Jingzhao, staffed a full bureaucracy, and levied the capital districts; within ten days fodder and grain were in hand.

sentences.zh: 乃陳兵下令曰：「國家多難，乘輿播遷，見危死節，自吾之分。

translations.literal: He then arrayed the troops and issued orders, saying, "The state has many hardships; the imperial carriage is cast adrift—to meet peril and die for principle is my own portion.
translations.idiomatic: He paraded his troops and proclaimed, "The realm is in crisis and the throne in exile—to face danger and die for duty is our portion.

sentences.zh: 公等此時不誅元兇，取富貴，非豪英也。

translations.literal: If you gentlemen at this time do not execute the chief culprit and seize wealth and honor, you are not heroes.
translations.idiomatic: If you will not now strike down the arch-rebel and win glory, you are no true warriors.

sentences.zh: 渭橋斷賊首尾，吾欲與公戮力一心，建不世之功，可乎？」

translations.literal: East Wei Bridge severs the rebels' head and tail; I wish to join you in one heart and united strength to establish an unexampled achievement—will you?
translations.idiomatic: At East Wei Bridge we can cut the enemy in two—I ask you to fight as one and win a fame that will never die. Will you follow me?

sentences.zh: 士皆雪泣曰：「惟公命。」

translations.literal: The soldiers all wept through snow and said, "Only your command."
translations.idiomatic: The men wept as one and cried, "We await only your word."

sentences.zh: 於是駱元光以華州之眾守潼關，尚可孤以神策兵保七盤，皆受晟節度；

translations.literal: Thereupon Luo Yuanguang with the forces of Huazhou guarded Tong Pass, Shang Ke'gu with Divine Strategy troops held Qipan—all under Sheng's command;
translations.idiomatic: Luo Yuanguang of Huazhou took Tong Pass, Shang Ke'gu held Qipan with Divine Strategy troops, and both came under Sheng's command;

sentences.zh: 戴休顏舉奉天，韓遊瑰悉邠寧軍從晟。

translations.literal: Dai Xiuyan raised Fengtian, and Han Yougui brought the entire Binning army to follow Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Xiuyan rallied Fengtian, and Han Yougui marched the whole Binning army to Sheng's side.

sentences.zh: 懷光始懼。

translations.literal: Huai'guang then began to fear.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang at last grew afraid.

sentences.zh: 晟乃移書顯讓之，使破賊自贖。

translations.literal: Sheng then sent an open letter rebuking him, urging him to break the rebels and redeem himself.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng sent him an open letter of rebuke, bidding him crush the rebels and redeem himself.

sentences.zh: 懷光不聽，然其下益攜落，畏為晟襲，乃奔河中。

translations.literal: Huai'guang would not listen, yet his subordinates grew ever more divided and falling away; fearing attack by Sheng, he then fled to Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang refused, but his ranks crumbled; fearing a strike by Sheng, he fled to Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 其將孟涉、段威勇以兵數千自拔歸，晟皆表以要官。

translations.literal: His generals Meng She and Duan Weiyong with several thousand troops broke away and returned; Sheng memorialized them all for important posts.
translations.idiomatic: Generals Meng She and Duan Weiyong defected with several thousand men, and Sheng recommended each for high office.

sentences.zh: 帝遣使者間道詔晟兼河中、晉絳慈隰節度使，又兼京畿、渭北、鄜坊、丹延節度招討使。

translations.literal: The emperor sent envoys by secret paths with edicts making Sheng concurrently military commissioner of Hezhong and Jin, Jiang, Ci, and Sui, and also concurrently pacification commissioner of the capital region, north of the Wei, Fufang, and Danyan.
translations.idiomatic: By secret courier the emperor named Sheng military commissioner of Hezhong and Jin-Jiang-Ci-Sui, and also pacification commissioner for the capital region, the Wei north bank, Fufang, and Danyan.

sentences.zh: 帝欲益西幸，晟請駐梁、漢以系天下望。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to go farther west; Sheng requested that he halt at Liang and Han to hold the world's hopes.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor planned to flee farther west, Sheng urged him to remain at Liang and Han to keep the empire's hopes fixed on the throne.

sentences.zh: 又進京畿、渭北、鄜坊、商華兵馬副元帥。

translations.literal: He was further promoted to Deputy Commander of troops for the capital region, north of the Wei, Fufang, and Shanghua.
translations.idiomatic: He was further made deputy commander of forces for the capital region, the Wei north bank, Fufang, and Shanghua.

sentences.zh: 時京兆司錄參軍李敬仲自賊中來，乃署節度府判官，以諫議大夫鄭雲逵為行軍司馬，擢張彧自副。

translations.literal: At the time Li Jingzhong, Registrar of Jingzhao, came from within the rebels; Sheng appointed him judge of the military commission headquarters, made Remonstrance Official Zheng Yunkui campaigning staff major, and promoted Zhang Yu as his own deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jingzhong, registrar of Jingzhao, escaped from the rebel-held city; Sheng made him chief secretary of headquarters, named Remonstrance Official Zheng Yunkui campaigning staff major, and elevated Zhang Yu to his own deputy.

sentences.zh: 神策軍及晟家皆為賊質，左右有言者，晟涕數行下，曰：「陛下安在，而欲恤家乎？」

translations.literal: The Divine Strategy Army and Sheng's family were all held hostage by the rebels; those around him spoke of it; Sheng shed several lines of tears and said, "Where is Your Majesty's safety, that I should care for family?
translations.idiomatic: The Divine Strategy Army and Sheng's own kin were hostages in rebel hands; when aides raised it, tears streamed down his face. "The emperor's fate is unknown," he said, "and you would have me fret over my household?

sentences.zh: 泚使晟吏王無忌婿款壁門曰：「公等家無恙。」

translations.literal: Zhu Ci sent the son-in-law of Sheng's officer Wang Wuji to knock at the camp gate, saying, "Your households are unharmed."
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci sent the son-in-law of Sheng's officer Wang Wuji to the gate with word that their families were safe.

sentences.zh: 晟怒曰：「爾乃與賊為間乎？」

translations.literal: Sheng angrily said, "Are you acting as go-between with the rebels?"
translations.idiomatic: Sheng thundered, "Are you spying for the enemy?"

sentences.zh: 叱斬之。

translations.literal: He shouted and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: He had the man executed on the spot.

sentences.zh: 時輸縑不屬，盛夏，士有衣裘者，晟能與下同其苦，以忠誼感發士心，終無攜怨。

translations.literal: At the time silk tribute did not arrive; in midsummer some soldiers wore fur coats; Sheng could share their hardship with the ranks, stirring their hearts with loyalty and righteousness, and in the end none harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Supplies of silk had run out; in the heat of summer some men still wore furs. Sheng shared their hardships and stirred them with loyalty until not one soldier turned mutinous.

sentences.zh: 邏士得姚令言、崔宣諜者，晟命釋縛，飯飲之，遣還，敕曰：「為我謝令言等，善為賊守，勿不忠於泚。」

translations.literal: Patrol soldiers captured spies of Yao Lingyan and Cui Xuan; Sheng ordered their bonds loosed, fed and watered them, and sent them back with instructions: "Bear my thanks to Lingyan and the rest—guard well for the rebels, and do not be disloyal to Zhu Ci."
translations.idiomatic: Patrols seized spies of Yao Lingyan and Cui Xuan; Sheng freed them, gave them food and drink, and sent them back with a message: "Tell Lingyan to keep faith with Zhu Ci and hold the city well for him."

sentences.zh: 乃引兵叩都門，賊不敢出，振旅而還。

translations.literal: He then led troops to knock at the capital gates; the rebels did not dare come out, and he reformed the ranks and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He marched to the capital gates; the rebels dared not sally forth, and he withdrew in good order.

sentences.zh: 明日，會諸將圖所向，眾對先拔外城，然後清宮。

translations.literal: The next day he convened the generals to plan direction; the assembly answered that they should first take the outer city, then clear the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Next day he called his generals to decide the plan; most urged taking the outer city first, then storming the palace.

sentences.zh: 晟曰：「外城有裏閈之隘，若設伏格戰，居人囂潰，非計也。

translations.literal: Sheng said, "The outer city has narrow lanes and wards; if we fight with ambushes in the streets, the inhabitants will panic and scatter—that is no plan.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng objected: "The outer wards are a maze of alleys; street fighting would panic the civilians—that is no strategy.

sentences.zh: 賊重兵精甲聚苑中，今直擊之，是披其心腹，將圖走不暇。」

translations.literal: The rebels' heavy troops and fine armor are gathered in the park; if we strike them directly now, we split open their heart and belly—they will plan flight and have no leisure.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy's best troops are massed in the imperial park; strike there and we pierce their heart—they will flee before they can think.

sentences.zh: 諸將曰：「善。」

translations.literal: The generals said, "Good."
translations.idiomatic: The generals agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃自東渭橋移壁光泰門，以薄都城，連溝柵。

translations.literal: He then moved his camp from East Wei Bridge to Guangtai Gate, pressing close to the capital, linking trenches and palisades.
translations.idiomatic: He shifted from East Wei Bridge to Guangtai Gate, pressed the capital, and linked trenches and stockades.

sentences.zh: 而賊將張庭芝、李希倩求戰，晟顧曰：「賊不出，是吾憂也。

translations.literal: The rebel generals Zhang Tingzhi and Li Xiqian sought battle; Sheng looked back and said, "If the rebels do not come out, that is my worry.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel generals Zhang Tingzhi and Li Xiqian offered battle; Sheng remarked, "My fear was that they would not come out.

sentences.zh: 今乃冒死來，天誘之矣。」

translations.literal: Now they rashly risk death and come—Heaven has lured them.
translations.idiomatic: Now they throw themselves into the fight—Heaven has delivered them to us.

sentences.zh: 勒吳詵等縱兵鏖擊。

translations.literal: He ordered Wu Shen and others to unleash the troops in fierce attack.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Wu Shen and the rest to charge.

sentences.zh: 賊攻華師急，晟以精騎馳救，中軍噪而從，大破之，乘勝入光泰門；

translations.literal: The rebels pressed Hua's division hard; Sheng galloped with elite cavalry to rescue; the center army shouted and followed, routing them greatly, and following victory entered Guangtai Gate;
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy hammered Hua's wing, Sheng raced in with elite cavalry; the center roared forward, broke them, and drove through Guangtai Gate;

sentences.zh: 再戰，敗卻，僵屍相藉，余眾走白華，賊大哭，終夜不息。

translations.literal: In a second battle they were defeated and driven back; corpses lay piled upon one another; the remainder fled to Baihua; the rebels wept loudly all night without cease.
translations.idiomatic: In a second clash the rebels broke; the dead lay in heaps; survivors fled to Baihua, and the enemy wailed through the night.

sentences.zh: 翌日，將復戰。

translations.literal: The next day they were about to fight again.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he prepared to attack again.

sentences.zh: 或請待西師，晟曰：「賊既敗，當乘機撲殄。

translations.literal: Some asked to wait for the western army; Sheng said, "The rebels are already defeated—we should seize the moment to crush and exterminate them.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged waiting for western reinforcements; Sheng said, "The enemy is broken—we must strike now and finish them.

sentences.zh: 苟俟西軍，是容其為計，豈吾利邪？」

translations.literal: If we wait for the western army, we allow them room to plot—how is that to our advantage?
translations.idiomatic: Wait for the western army and we give them time to recover—where is the gain in that?

sentences.zh: 乃悉軍軍光泰門，使王佖、李演將騎，史萬頃將步，抵苑北。

translations.literal: He then marshaled the whole army at Guangtai Gate, made Wang Tian and Li Yan lead cavalry, Shi Wanqing lead infantry, and reached the north of the park.
translations.idiomatic: He massed the whole army at Guangtai Gate, Wang Tian and Li Yan leading the horse, Shi Wanqing the foot, and advanced to the north of the imperial park.

sentences.zh: 晟先夜隤苑垣為道二百步，比兵至，賊已伐木塞以拒戰。

translations.literal: Sheng had the night before breached the park wall for a passage two hundred paces wide; by the time the troops arrived, the rebels had felled trees to block and resist battle.
translations.idiomatic: Overnight Sheng had breached two hundred paces of the park wall; when his men arrived, the rebels had already felled trees to block the way.

sentences.zh: 晟叱諸將曰：「安得縱賊？

translations.literal: Sheng shouted at the generals, "How can you let the rebels go?
translations.idiomatic: Sheng roared at his generals, "How dare you let the enemy escape!

sentences.zh: 今先斬公矣！」

translations.literal: I will behead you first!
translations.idiomatic: I will execute you myself first!

sentences.zh: 萬頃懼，先登，拔柵以入，佖督騎繼之。

translations.literal: Wanqing in fear climbed first, tore down the palisade and entered; Tian directed the cavalry to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Wanqing led the assault, tore down the barricade, and broke in; Tian drove the cavalry after him.

sentences.zh: 賊崩潰，執其將段誠諫，大兵分道進，雷噪震地。

translations.literal: The rebels collapsed; they seized the general Duan Chengjian; the great army advanced by separate routes, thunderous noise shaking the ground.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel line shattered; Duan Chengjian was captured; the main force swept in on every road with a roar that shook the earth.

sentences.zh: 令言、庭芝、希倩等殊死鬥，晟令唐良臣等步騎奔突，賊陣成輒北，十餘遇皆不勝，蹙入白華。

translations.literal: Lingyan, Tingzhi, Xiqian and others fought to the death; Sheng ordered Tang Liangchen and others with foot and horse to charge; whenever the rebel line formed it turned north; more than ten encounters all went against them, and they were pressed into Baihua.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyan, Tingzhi, and Xiqian fought desperately; Sheng sent Tang Liangchen's mixed force to hammer them; ten times the rebels formed line and ten times they broke, driven at last into Baihua.

sentences.zh: 賊伏千騎出官軍背，晟以麾下百騎自馳之，左右呼曰：「相公來！」

translations.literal: The rebels hid a thousand horsemen to strike the government army from behind; Sheng with a hundred horsemen of his suite galloped at them himself; those at his side cried, "The Chancellor comes!
translations.idiomatic: A thousand rebel horsemen ambushed the government rear; Sheng himself charged with a hundred riders while his men shouted, "The Chancellor comes!

sentences.zh: 賊驚潰，禽馘略盡。

translations.literal: The rebels in alarm collapsed; prisoners and severed ears were nearly all taken.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy panicked and fled; prisoners and heads were taken by the score.

sentences.zh: 泚率殘卒萬人西走，田子奇追之，餘黨悉降。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci led ten thousand remnant soldiers west in flight; Tian Ziqi pursued them, and the remaining factions all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci fled west with ten thousand survivors; Tian Ziqi pursued, and the rest surrendered.

sentences.zh: 晟引軍屯含元外廷，舍右金吾次，令軍中曰：「五日內不得輒通家問，違者斬。」

translations.literal: Sheng led the army to encamp in the outer court of Hanyuan, lodging at the Right Golden Crow station, and ordered the army: "Within five days none may casually send word home—violators will be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng quartered his troops in the outer court of Hanyuan Hall and proclaimed: "For five days no man may send word home—on pain of death.

sentences.zh: 遣京兆尹李齊運部長安、萬年令，分慰居人，秋毫無所擾。

translations.literal: He sent Jingzhao Magistrate Li Qiyun to deploy the magistrates of Chang'an and Wannian to comfort residents separately, not disturbing so much as an autumn hair.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Li Qiyun, magistrate of Jingzhao, with the county magistrates to reassure the populace; not a household was molested.

sentences.zh: 別將高明曜取賊妓一，司馬伷取賊馬二，即斬以徇。

translations.literal: Separate commander Gao Mingyao took one rebel courtesan; staff major You took two rebel horses—they were immediately beheaded as warning.
translations.idiomatic: When subcommander Gao Mingyao seized a rebel woman and staff major You two rebel horses, Sheng had them executed as an example.

sentences.zh: 坊人之遠者，宿昔乃知王師之入也。

translations.literal: Residents of distant wards only after a night and day learned that the royal army had entered.
translations.idiomatic: In distant wards people only learned a day later that the imperial army had taken the city.

sentences.zh: 明日，孟涉屯白華，尚可孤屯望仙門，駱元光屯章敬寺，晟屯安國寺。

translations.literal: The next day Meng She encamped at Baihua, Shang Ke'gu at Wangxian Gate, Luo Yuanguang at Zhangjing Temple, and Sheng at Anguo Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Next day Meng She held Baihua, Shang Ke'gu Wangxian Gate, Luo Yuanguang Zhangjing Temple, and Sheng Anguo Temple.

sentences.zh: 斬賊用事者及臣賊宦豎於市，表著節不屈者，擇文武攝台省官，以俟乘輿。

translations.literal: He beheaded rebel agents and eunuch minions who served the rebels in the market, posted lists of those who kept integrity and did not yield, and selected civil and military men to act as provisional officials of the central ministries, awaiting the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: He executed rebel officials and collaborating eunuchs in public, honored those who had refused to submit, and appointed civil and military men to hold the central ministries until the emperor's return.

sentences.zh: 條脅汙於賊者，請以不死。

translations.literal: He listed those coerced and defiled by the rebels and requested that they not be put to death.
translations.idiomatic: He drew up a list of those forced into service under the rebels and pleaded that their lives be spared.

sentences.zh: 露布至梁，帝感泣，群臣上壽，且言：「晟蕩夷凶憝，而市不易廛，宗廟不震，長安之人不識旗鼓，雖三代用師，不能加之。」

translations.literal: When the victory bulletin reached Liang, the emperor wept with emotion; the ministers offered longevity congratulations and moreover said, "Sheng swept away fierce villains, yet the markets did not change their stalls, the ancestral temples were not shaken, and the people of Chang'an did not know banners and drums—even the Three Dynasties in employing armies could not surpass this.
translations.idiomatic: When the victory dispatch reached Liangzhou the emperor wept; at court the ministers praised Sheng for crushing the rebels without disturbing the markets, the temples, or the people of Chang'an—a feat, they said, beyond even the sage kings of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「天生晟，為社稷萬人，豈獨朕哉！」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Heaven gave birth to Sheng for the altars of state and the myriad people—how is it for me alone!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Heaven sent us Sheng for the realm and its people—not for my sake alone!"

sentences.zh: 拜晟司徒，兼中書令，實封千戶。

translations.literal: He appointed Sheng Minister of Education and Concurrent Grand Councilor, with a substantive fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng was made Minister of Education and Grand Councilor, with a substantive fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 晟遣大將吳詵以兵三千到寶雞清道，自請迎扈，不許。

translations.literal: Sheng sent Grand General Wu Shen with three thousand troops to Baoji to clear the road, and himself requested to come and escort the emperor—this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng sent Wu Shen with three thousand men to clear the road at Baoji and asked leave to escort the emperor home; the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 帝至自梁，晟以戎服見三橋，帝駐馬勞之。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned from Liang, Sheng in military dress met him at San Bridge; the emperor halted his horse and comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned from Liangzhou, Sheng met him at San Bridge in armor; the emperor reined in and praised him.

sentences.zh: 晟再拜頓首，賀克殄大盜，廟朝安復，已，即跪陳：「備爪牙臣，不能指日破賊，致乘輿再狩，乃臣不任職之咎，敢請死。」

translations.literal: Sheng bowed twice and knocked his head, congratulating on exterminating the great bandits and restoring the temples and court; then he knelt and stated, "As a minister prepared to be claws and fangs, I could not break the rebels within days, causing the imperial carriage to hunt again—it is my fault for not fulfilling duty; I dare request death.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng bowed low, hailed the destruction of the rebels and the restoration of court and capital, then knelt and said, "Your servant failed to crush the rebels in time and forced Your Majesty into exile again—the fault is mine alone; I beg for death.

sentences.zh: 伏道左，帝為掩涕，命給事中齊映起之，使就位。

translations.literal: He prostrated himself to the left of the road; the emperor wiped away tears and ordered Attendant Gentleman Qi Ying to raise him and have him take his place.
translations.idiomatic: He lay prostrate beside the road; the emperor wiped his eyes and ordered Qi Ying to raise him and take his station.

sentences.zh: 有詔賜第永崇裏、涇陽上田、延平門之林園、女樂一列。

translations.literal: An edict granted him a mansion in Yongchong Lane, superior fields in Jingyang, the grove and garden at Yanping Gate, and a troupe of female musicians.
translations.idiomatic: By edict he received a mansion in Yongchong Lane, choice fields in Jingyang, the gardens at Yanping Gate, and a company of musicians.

sentences.zh: 晟入第，京兆供帳，教坊鼓吹迎導，詔將相送之。

translations.literal: When Sheng entered his mansion, Jingzhao supplied furnishings; the Music Office with drums and pipes welcomed and guided him; an edict ordered chancellors and ministers to escort him.
translations.idiomatic: When he entered his new house, Jingzhao furnished it, the imperial musicians escorted him in state, and the chancellors were ordered to attend him home.

sentences.zh: 帝紀其功，自文於碑，敕皇太子書，立於東渭橋，以示後世雲。

translations.literal: The emperor recorded his merit, himself composing the text on the stele, ordering the Crown Prince to write it, and erecting it at East Wei Bridge to show posterity.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor composed the inscription himself, had the crown prince write it on stone, and set it up at East Wei Bridge for generations to see.

sentences.zh: 又令太子錄副以賜。

translations.literal: He also ordered the Crown Prince to copy a duplicate to bestow.
translations.idiomatic: He also had the crown prince copy the text and present it to Sheng as a gift.

sentences.zh: 始，晟屯渭橋也，熒惑守歲，久乃退，府中皆賀曰：「熒惑退，國家之利，速用兵者昌。」

translations.literal: At the beginning, when Sheng encamped at Wei Bridge, the Sparkling Deluder guarded the year star; after long it withdrew, and everyone in headquarters congratulated him, saying, "When the Sparkling Deluder withdraws, it is the state's advantage—he who swiftly uses troops will prosper.
translations.idiomatic: While Sheng was at Wei Bridge, Mars had lingered in the heavens; when it finally moved off, his staff congratulated him: "Mars retreats—a blessing for the state; swift action will bring victory.

sentences.zh: 晟曰：「天子暴露，人臣當力死勤難，安知天道邪？」

translations.literal: Sheng said, "The Son of Heaven is exposed to the elements; as subjects we should exert strength unto death in hard service—how do we know the Way of Heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: Sheng replied, "The emperor suffers in the open; a subject owes his life in hardship—what has astrology to do with it?"

sentences.zh: 至是，乃曰：「前士大夫勸晟出兵，非敢拒也。

translations.literal: At this time he then said, "Formerly the scholar-officials urged Sheng to send out troops—I did not dare refuse.
translations.idiomatic: Only now he explained, "When my officers urged me to attack, I did not refuse them out of fear.

sentences.zh: 且人可用而不可使之知也。

translations.literal: Moreover, men may be used but must not be made to know.
translations.idiomatic: Men can be led, but they must not be told the whole truth.

sentences.zh: 夫惟五緯盈縮不常，晟懼復守歲，則我軍不戰自屈矣！」

translations.literal: For the Five Planets wax and wane without constancy; Sheng feared that if Mars again guarded the year star, our army would yield without fighting!
translations.idiomatic: The planets shift unpredictably; I feared that if Mars returned, the men would lose heart without a blow being struck!

sentences.zh: 皆曰：「非所及也。」

translations.literal: All said, "That is beyond what we could reach."
translations.idiomatic: All agreed they would never have thought of it.

sentences.zh: 涇州倚邊，數戕其帥，晟請治不龔命者，因以訓耕積粟實塞下，羈制西戎。

translations.literal: Jingzhou leaned on the border and repeatedly killed its commanders; Sheng requested to punish those who did not respect orders, and thereby train farming and amass grain to fill the frontier, restraining the Western Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhou on the frontier had seen one commander after another murdered; Sheng asked to punish the disobedient, promote farming, stock the border granaries, and hold the western tribes in check.

sentences.zh: 帝乃拜晟鳳翔、隴右、涇原節度使，兼行營副元帥，徙王西平郡，實封千五百戶。

translations.literal: The emperor then appointed Sheng military commissioner of Fengxiang, Longyou, and Jingyuan, and concurrent deputy commander of the campaigning army, transferring his princedom to Xiping Commandery with a substantive fief of one thousand five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made him commissioner of Fengxiang, Longyou, and Jingyuan, deputy supreme commander of the field armies, and Prince of Xiping with a fief of fifteen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 晟請與李楚琳俱行，亦將治殺張鎰罪，帝方務安反側，不許。

translations.literal: Sheng requested to go together with Li Chulin and also to punish the crime of killing Zhang Yi; the emperor was then bent on pacifying the rebellious, and did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng asked to take Li Chulin with him and to punish Zhang Yi's murderers; the emperor, seeking to pacify former rebels, refused.

sentences.zh: 晟至鳳翔，亂將王斌等十餘人以次伏誅。

translations.literal: When Sheng reached Fengxiang, more than ten mutinous generals including Wang Bin were in turn executed.
translations.idiomatic: At Fengxiang he executed more than a dozen mutinous officers, Wang Bin among them.

sentences.zh: 時宦者尹元貞持節到同、華，擅入河中諭慰李懷光。

translations.literal: At the time the eunuch Yin Yuanzhen bore credentials to Tong and Hua and on his own authority entered Hezhong to instruct and comfort Li Huai'guang.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Yin Yuanzhen, credentialed for Tong and Hua, had entered Hezhong on his own to parley with Li Huai'guang.

sentences.zh: 晟劾元貞矯使，欲洗宥元惡，請治罪。

translations.literal: Sheng impeached Yuanzhen for forging the mission, wishing to whitewash and pardon the chief villain, and requested punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng impeached Yin for exceeding his commission and seeking to absolve the arch-traitor, demanding his punishment.

sentences.zh: 又言：「赦懷光有五不可：河中抵京師三百里，同州制其沖，兵多則示未信，少則力不足，忽驚東偏，何以待之？

translations.literal: He also said, "To pardon Huai'guang has five impossibilities: Hezhong is three hundred li from the capital; Tongzhou controls its crossing; many troops show lack of trust, few show insufficient strength—if the eastern flank is suddenly alarmed, how shall we meet it?
translations.idiomatic: He added five reasons not to pardon Huai'guang: "Hezhong lies three hundred li from the capital; Tongzhou commands its approach; a large garrison shows distrust, a small one is too weak—if the east is suddenly threatened, how will we respond?

sentences.zh: 一也。

translations.literal: That is the first.
translations.idiomatic: That is the first.

sentences.zh: 今赦懷光，則必以晉、絳、慈、隰還之，渾瑊、康日知又且遷徙，二也。

translations.literal: If we now pardon Huai'guang, we must return Jin, Jiang, Ci, and Sui to him, and Hun Jian and Kang Rizhi must again be transferred—that is the second.
translations.idiomatic: Pardon him and we must return Jin, Jiang, Ci, and Sui; Hun Jian and Kang Rizhi would have to be moved again—the second reason.

sentences.zh: 兵力未窮，忽宥反逆，四夷聞之，謂陛下兵屈而自罷耳；

translations.literal: Military strength is not exhausted, yet suddenly pardoning a rebel—the Four Barbarians hearing it will say Your Majesty's armies bent and withdrew of themselves;
translations.idiomatic: Our strength is not spent, yet we pardon a traitor—the border peoples will think Your Majesty's armies broke and quit of their own accord;

sentences.zh: 今回紇拒北，吐蕃梗西，希烈僭淮、蔡，若棄強示弱，以招窺覬，三也。

translations.literal: now the Uyghurs block the north, Tibet obstructs the west, and Xilie usurps Huai and Cai—if we abandon strength to show weakness and invite covetous eyes, that is the third.
translations.idiomatic: with the Uyghurs in the north, Tibet in the west, and Xilie in Huai and Cai—to show weakness now is to invite attack—the third reason.

sentences.zh: 懷光既赦，則朔方將士悉復敘勳行賞，追還縑廩；

translations.literal: If Huai'guang is pardoned, then the Shuofang officers and soldiers will all again have merits recorded and rewards distributed, and silk and rations will be reclaimed;
translations.idiomatic: Pardon Huai'guang and every Shuofang soldier will demand back pay and rewards;

sentences.zh: 今府庫空殫，物不酬滿，是激其叛，四也。

translations.literal: now the treasuries are empty and exhausted, goods cannot repay in full—this stirs them to rebel; that is the fourth.
translations.idiomatic: the treasury is empty and cannot satisfy them—that will provoke fresh rebellion—the fourth.

sentences.zh: 既解河中，諸道還屯，當有賜賚，賞典不舉，怨言必起，五也。

translations.literal: Once Hezhong is relieved, the various circuits return to garrison and ought to receive gifts and grants; if the reward canon is not carried out, complaints will surely arise—that is the fifth.
translations.idiomatic: Relieve Hezhong and every circuit that marched will expect rewards; fail to grant them and muttering will turn to mutiny—the fifth.

sentences.zh: 今河中米鬥五百，芻稿且罄，人餓死牆壁間，其大將殺戮幾盡，圍之旬時，力窮且潰，願無養腹心疾為後憂。

translations.literal: Now in Hezhong rice is five hundred per dou, fodder and straw are nearly exhausted, people starve to death between walls; their great generals are killed almost to the last; besiege them ten days and more and their strength is spent and they will collapse—I wish you not to nourish a disease of the vitals as a later worry.
translations.idiomatic: Rice in Hezhong costs five hundred cash a peck; fodder is gone and men starve in the streets; his generals are nearly all dead; another ten days of siege and he will break. Do not spare a mortal enemy to trouble us later.

sentences.zh: 臣請選精兵五千，約十日糧，可以破賊。」

translations.literal: Your servant requests to select five thousand elite troops with about ten days' provisions—we can break the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Give me five thousand picked men and ten days' rations, and I will destroy him.

sentences.zh: 帝方以賊委馬燧、渾瑊，故不許。

translations.literal: The emperor was then entrusting the rebels to Ma Sui and Hun Jian, and therefore did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had already assigned the campaign to Ma Sui and Hun Jian and refused.

sentences.zh: 晟至涇而田希鑒迎謁，執之，並其党石奇等悉伏誅。

translations.literal: When Sheng reached Jing, Tian Xijian came to meet and pay respects; he seized him, and together with his faction Shi Qi and others all were executed.
translations.idiomatic: At Jingzhou Tian Xijian came out to greet him; Sheng seized him and executed him along with his accomplice Shi Qi and the rest.

sentences.zh: 表右龍武將軍李觀為涇原節度使。

translations.literal: He memorialized Right Dragon Martial General Li Guan as military commissioner of Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Li Guan, general of the Right Dragon Martial Army, as commissioner of Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 晟常曰：「河、隴之陷，非吐蕃能取之，皆將臣遝貪，暴其種落，不得耕稼，日益東徙，自棄之爾。

translations.literal: Sheng often said, "The fall of He and Long was not that the Tibetans could take them—all came from generals and ministers being greedy in succession, oppressing their tribes, preventing farming, daily moving eastward—we abandoned it ourselves.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng often said, "We lost the He-Long region not because Tibet was too strong, but because our officers plundered the tribes, ruined their fields, and drove them east—we threw the land away ourselves.

sentences.zh: 且土無繒絮，人苦役擾，思唐之心，豈有既乎？」

translations.literal: Moreover the land lacks silk and cotton wadding; the people suffer from corvée and harassment—the heart that longs for Tang, how could it have an end?
translations.idiomatic: They lack cloth and suffer under our levies—their longing for Tang will never die.

sentences.zh: 因悉家貲懷輯降附，得大酋浪息曩，表以王號。

translations.literal: Thereupon he used all his family wealth to embrace and gather those who surrendered, obtained the great chieftain Langxi'nang, and memorialized to grant him a princely title.
translations.idiomatic: He spent his private fortune to win over defectors, took the great chief Langxi'nang under his protection, and had him enfeoffed as a prince.

sentences.zh: 每虜使至，必召息曩於坐，衣大錦袍、金帶，誇異之，虜皆指目歆豔。

translations.literal: Whenever barbarian envoys came, he always summoned Xi'nang to the seat, clothed in a great brocade robe and golden belt, displaying him with wonder; the barbarians all pointed and gazed with eager admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Tibetan envoys came, he seated Langxi'nang beside him in brocade and gold, a living proof of Tang favor, to the envy of every visitor.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃君臣大懼，相與議。

translations.literal: The Tibetan ruler and ministers were greatly afraid and deliberated together.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetan court was alarmed and held council.

sentences.zh: 尚結贊者善計，乃曰：「唐名將特李晟與馬燧、渾瑊爾，不去之，必為吾患。」

translations.literal: Shang Jiezan was skilled in stratagem and thus said, "Among Tang's famous generals there are only Li Sheng, Ma Sui, and Hun Jian—if we do not remove them, they will surely be our trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Jiezan, their strategist, said, "Tang has only three great generals—Li Sheng, Ma Sui, and Hun Jian. Until they are removed, they will plague us.

sentences.zh: 即遣使委辭，因燧請和，且求盟，因盟謀執瑊以賣燧，於是結贊大興兵逾隴、岐，無所掠，陽怒曰：「召吾來，乃不牛酒犒軍。」

translations.literal: He then sent envoys with humble words, through Sui requesting peace and moreover seeking alliance; under cover of alliance he plotted to seize Jian and betray Sui; thereupon Jiezan greatly raised troops crossing Long and Qi, finding nothing to plunder, and feigned anger, saying, "You summoned us here, yet give no cattle and wine to comfort the army."
translations.idiomatic: He sent humble envoys through Ma Sui to sue for peace and an alliance, planning to seize Hun Jian at the treaty table and turn Ma Sui against Li Sheng. Jiezan marched in force through Long and Qi, found little booty, and pretended outrage: "You invited us and offer no feast for our men."

sentences.zh: 徐引去。

translations.literal: He slowly led his forces away.
translations.idiomatic: Then he withdrew slowly.

sentences.zh: 以是間晟。

translations.literal: By this he sowed discord regarding Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Thus he sowed suspicion between Sheng and the court.

sentences.zh: 晟選兵三千，使王佖伏汧陽旁，擊其中軍，幾獲結贊。

translations.literal: Sheng selected three thousand troops and made Wang Tian lie in ambush beside Qianyang, striking their center army and nearly capturing Jiezan.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng sent three thousand men with Wang Tian to ambush near Qianyang, struck the Tibetan center, and nearly took Jiezan himself.

sentences.zh: 晟又遣野詩良輔等攻摧沙堡，拔之。

translations.literal: Sheng also sent Ye Shi Liangfu and others to attack and destroy Shabo Fort and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Ye Shi Liangfu to storm Shabo Fort and take it.

sentences.zh: 結贊屢乞和，會晟朝京師，奏言：「戎狄無信，不可許。」

translations.literal: Jiezan repeatedly begged for peace; when Sheng attended court at the capital he memorialized, saying, "The Rong and Di are faithless—it cannot be permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Jiezan repeatedly sued for peace; when Sheng came to court he warned, "The barbarians are not to be trusted—do not agree.

sentences.zh: 宰相韓滉與晟合，因請調軍食以給西師。

translations.literal: Grand Councilor Han Huang agreed with Sheng and therefore requested to transfer military grain to supply the western army.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Han Huang sided with Sheng and urged shipping grain to the western armies.

sentences.zh: 然天子內厭兵，疑將臣生事。

translations.literal: Yet the Son of Heaven inwardly wearied of warfare and suspected the generals and ministers of stirring trouble.
translations.idiomatic: But the emperor had grown weary of war and suspected his generals of seeking trouble.

sentences.zh: 亦會滉卒而張延賞當國，故與晟有隙，後雖詔講解，而陰不與也，密言晟不可久持兵，更薦劉玄佐、李抱真經略西北，俾立功以間晟。

translations.literal: It also happened that Huang died and Zhang Yanshang held the state; he had an old rift with Sheng; though later an edict urged reconciliation, in secret he was not reconciled, secretly saying Sheng must not long hold troops, and further recommending Liu Xuanzuo and Li Baozhen to manage the northwest, causing them to achieve merit so as to come between Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Huang died, Zhang Yanshang took power; he and Sheng were old enemies. Though the court ordered peace between them, Zhang secretly urged that Sheng must not keep an army, and pushed Liu Xuanzuo and Li Baozhen to win glory in the northwest and eclipse him.

sentences.zh: 帝惑其言。

translations.literal: The emperor was swayed by his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor believed him.

sentences.zh: 貞元三年，帝坐宣政殿引見晟，備冊禮，進拜太尉、中書令，罷其兵。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenyuan, the emperor sat in Xuanzheng Hall and received Sheng in audience with full investiture rites, promoting him to Grand Marshal and Grand Councilor and dismissing his military command.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan year 3 the emperor received Sheng in Xuanzheng Hall with full ceremonial honors, made him Grand Marshal and Grand Councilor, and stripped him of his army.

sentences.zh: 詔晟乘輅謁太廟，視事尚書省，賜良馬、錦彩千計。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Sheng to ride the imperial carriage to visit the Grand Temple, conduct affairs at the Department of State Affairs, and bestowed fine horses and brocades by the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to ride in state to the ancestral temple, take up civil duties at the Department of State Affairs, and received thousands of horses and rolls of brocade.

sentences.zh: 是歲，瑊與吐蕃盟平涼，虜劫之，瑊挺身免，詔罷燧河東，皆如結贊計雲。

translations.literal: That year Jian allied with Tibet at Pingliang; the barbarians seized him, but Jian escaped by his own body; an edict dismissed Sui from Hedong—all as Jiezan's stratagem had planned.
translations.idiomatic: That year Hun Jian was seized at a peace conference at Pingliang but escaped alive; Ma Sui was removed from Hedong—all as Shang Jiezan had schemed.

sentences.zh: 通王府長史丁瓊者，嘗為延賞擠抑，內怨望，乃見晟曰：「以公功，乃奪兵柄，夫惟位高者難全，盍早圖之？」

translations.literal: Ding Qiong, chief administrator of the Prince of Tong's household, had once been suppressed by Yanshang and harbored resentment within; he then saw Sheng and said, "For your merit they yet took away military authority—only those of high position are hard to preserve intact—why not plan early?
translations.idiomatic: Ding Qiong, chief administrator of the Prince of Tong's household, nursed a grudge against Zhang Yanshang and came to Sheng: "After all your service they took your command—great men rarely die in bed. Should you not act while you can?

sentences.zh: 晟曰：「君安得不祥之言？」

translations.literal: Sheng said, "How can you speak such ill-omened words?"
translations.idiomatic: Sheng said, "How dare you speak treason to me?"

sentences.zh: 執以聞。

translations.literal: He seized him and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: He had Ding arrested and reported the matter to the throne.

sentences.zh: 明年，詔為晟立五廟，追賁高祖芝以下祔其主，給牲器床幄，禮官相事。

translations.literal: The next year an edict established five temples for Sheng, posthumously ennobling High Ancestor Zhi and below to be enshrined with their lord, supplying sacrificial vessels, beds, and curtains, with ritual officials assisting the affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Next year the court authorized five ancestral temples for Sheng, ennobling his forebears back to High Ancestor Zhi and supplying ritual officers and furnishings.

sentences.zh: 它日，與馬燧見延英，帝嘉其勳，下詔曰：「昔我烈祖，乘乾坤蕩滌，掃隋季荒茀，體元禦極，作人父母。

translations.literal: Another day, with Ma Sui he was received at Yanying; the emperor praised their merit and issued an edict saying, "Formerly our august ancestor, riding the cleansing of Heaven and Earth, swept away the wasteland of the Sui season's end, embodied the primal and ascended to the ultimate, becoming father and mother to the people.
translations.idiomatic: On another day he and Ma Sui were received in Yanying Hall; the emperor praised their service and proclaimed: "Our founding emperor, when Heaven and Earth were in turmoil, swept away the ruins of Sui and took the throne as father and mother to the people.

sentences.zh: 則有熊羆之士，不二心之臣，左右經綸，參翊締構，昭文德，恢武功，威不若，康不乂，用端命于上帝，付畀四方。

translations.literal: Then there were warriors like bears and brown bears, ministers of undivided heart, at left and right ordering the realm, assisting in founding and building, displaying civil virtue, restoring martial achievement—where awe was lacking, peace was not governed—thus receiving the upright mandate from High God and entrusting the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: At his side stood warriors fierce as bears and ministers of undivided loyalty, who ordered the realm, helped build the state, spread civil virtue and restored martial glory, brought order where there was none, received Heaven's mandate, and entrusted the empire to the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 王業既成，太階既平，乃圖厥容，列于淩煙閣，懋昭績效，表式儀形，以弗忘朝夕，永垂乎來裔。

translations.literal: When the royal enterprise was accomplished and the Great Steps were level, then their likenesses were painted and arrayed in the Lingyan Pavilion, greatly displaying achievements, expressing model forms, so as not to forget morning and evening, forever handed down to coming descendants.
translations.idiomatic: When the dynasty was secure and the realm at peace, their portraits were painted for the Lingyan Pavilion, their deeds made luminous, their forms held up as models, never to be forgotten, and handed down to all posterity.

sentences.zh: 君臣之義，厚莫重焉。

translations.literal: The righteousness between ruler and minister—none is heavier.
translations.idiomatic: No bond is weightier than that between sovereign and minister.

sentences.zh: 歲在己巳秋九月，我行西宮，瞻望崇構，見老臣遺像，顒然肅然，和敬在色。

translations.literal: The year being jisi, autumn, ninth month, I walked the Western Palace, gazed up at the lofty structure, and saw the surviving portraits of old ministers—dignified and solemn, harmony and reverence in their bearing.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of autumn in the jisi year I went to the Western Palace, looked up at the great hall, and saw the portraits of former ministers—grave, dignified faces full of harmony and respect.

sentences.zh: 想雲龍之協期，感致業之艱難，睹往思今，取類非遠。

translations.literal: I thought of the time when cloud and dragon joined in accord, felt the hardship of founding the enterprise, saw the past and thought on the present—the parallel is not far.
translations.idiomatic: I recalled the day when liege and servant stood together, felt again how hard it was to build the realm, and looking from past to present found the lesson close at hand.

sentences.zh: 且功與時並，才與世生，苟蘊其才，遇其時，尊主庇人，何代蔑有？

translations.literal: Moreover merit keeps pace with the age and talent is born with the times; if one stores talent and meets the time, honoring the lord and sheltering the people—what age has lacked them?
translations.idiomatic: Merit rises with its age and talent appears when the world needs it; wherever ability meets opportunity, men who exalt their sovereign and shield the people have never been wanting in any generation.

sentences.zh: 在中宗時，有如桓彥範等，著輔戴之績；

translations.literal: In the time of Zhongzong there were such as Huan Yanfan, who achieved the merit of assisting and upholding the ruler;
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Zhongzong, men like Huan Yanfan won fame for helping to restore the throne;

sentences.zh: 在玄宗時，有如劉幽求等，申弼翼之勳；

translations.literal: in the time of Xuanzong there were such as Liu Youqiu, who displayed the achievement of aiding and supporting;
translations.idiomatic: under Emperor Xuanzong, Liu Youqiu and others earned merit as loyal supporters;

sentences.zh: 在肅宗時，有如郭子儀，掃除氛祲。

translations.literal: in the time of Suzong there was such as Guo Ziyi, who swept away the baleful vapors.
translations.idiomatic: and under Emperor Suzong, Guo Ziyi cleared away the clouds of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 今顧晟等，保寧朕躬，咸宣力肆勤，光復宗祏，訂之前烈，夫豈多謝。

translations.literal: Now looking to Sheng and the rest, who secure and settle my person, all alike exerting strength and spreading diligence, restoring the ancestral altars—compared with the former worthies, how can thanks be enough?
translations.idiomatic: Today Li Sheng and his peers have kept me safe, every one of them straining in loyal service until the imperial house was restored—set beside those earlier heroes, words of thanks fall short.

sentences.zh: 闕而未錄，孰旌厥賢？

translations.literal: If omitted and not recorded, who will display their worth?
translations.idiomatic: If we leave them out of the record, how will their virtue be honored?

sentences.zh: 況念功紀德，文祖所為也，在予其曷敢怠？

translations.literal: Moreover to commemorate merit and record virtue is what the civil ancestor did—in me how dare I be idle?
translations.idiomatic: To remember service and inscribe virtue was the way of our civil founding emperor; how could I, in his place, dare to neglect it?

sentences.zh: 有司宜敘先後，各圖其象於舊臣之次。」

translations.literal: The responsible officials should arrange them in order of precedence, each painting their likeness in the place of the former ministers."
translations.idiomatic: Let the proper offices rank them in due order and paint each portrait in the gallery beside those of earlier ministers."

sentences.zh: 命皇太子書其文以賜晟，晟刻石於門。

translations.literal: He ordered the Crown Prince to write out the text and bestow it on Sheng; Sheng had it carved in stone at his gate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had the crown prince copy the edict as a gift to Sheng, and Sheng had the text engraved on stone at his gate.

sentences.zh: 七年，以臨洮未復，請附貫萬年，詔可。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, because Lintao had not yet been recovered, he requested attachment to Wan nian County; an edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, with Lintao still unrestored, he asked that his household be registered in Wan nian County, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 九年，薨，年六十七。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he died, aged sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he died, at sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 帝聞流涕，詔百官就第進吊。

translations.literal: The emperor, on hearing, shed tears and ordered the hundred officials to go to the residence and offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached him the emperor wept and ordered the whole bureaucracy to call at his home and mourn.

sentences.zh: 比大斂，帝手詔，誓以存保世嗣，申告柩前。

translations.literal: At the great encoffining the emperor personally drafted an edict, swearing to preserve and protect the heirs of the age, and proclaimed it before the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: At the lying-in-state the emperor wrote an edict in his own hand, pledging to guard Sheng's descendants, and read it aloud before the bier.

sentences.zh: 冊贈太師，諡曰忠武。

translations.literal: By patent he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor, with posthumous title Loyal Martial.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor with the temple name Loyal Martial.

sentences.zh: 及葬，又禦望春門臨送，遣謁者宣詔于柩車，百官拜哭於道。

translations.literal: At the burial he again went in person to Wangchun Gate to see him off, sent a Herald to proclaim the edict at the coffin cart, and the hundred officials bowed and wept along the road.
translations.idiomatic: At the funeral the emperor himself went to Wangchun Gate to see the procession off, sent a herald to read the edict beside the hearse, and officials lined the road, bowing and weeping.

sentences.zh: 憲宗元和中，詔其家與屬籍，以晟配饗德宗廟廷。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era of Xianzong an edict registered his household in the clan genealogy and paired Sheng in sacrifice at Dezong's temple hall.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Xianzong's Yuanhe reign his family was entered in the imperial genealogy and Li Sheng was given a place in the sacrifices at Emperor Dezong's temple.

sentences.zh: 僖宗狩蜀，倉部員外郎袁皓采晟功烈，為《興元聖功錄》，遍賜諸將，表勵之。

translations.literal: When Xizong hunted in Shu, Yuan Hao, an outer-office secretary in the Ministry of Revenue, gathered Sheng's achievements into the Record of Sacred Merit at Xingyuan and distributed it widely to the generals as encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xizong fled to Shu, Yuan Hao of the Revenue Bureau compiled Sheng's deeds into the Record of Sacred Merit at Xingyuan and sent copies to every general to stir them to emulation.

sentences.zh: 晟性疾惡，臨下明。

translations.literal: Sheng by nature hated evil fiercely and was clear toward those below.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng detested wickedness and was sharp and fair with his subordinates.

sentences.zh: 每治軍，必曰：「某有勞，某長於是。」

translations.literal: Whenever he regulated the army he would say, "So-and-so has merit; so-and-so excels at this."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he reviewed the troops he would say, "This man has earned credit; that one is best at such-and-such."

sentences.zh: 雖廝養小善，必記姓名，尤惡下為朋黨者。

translations.literal: Even small merits of grooms and servants he must record by name, and he especially hated subordinates who formed factions.
translations.idiomatic: Even a groom's small good deed he would note by name, and he loathed cliques among the ranks.

sentences.zh: 篤分義，隆於故舊。

translations.literal: He was deep in sharing righteousness and generous toward old friends.
translations.idiomatic: He was steadfast in friendship and lavish with old companions.

sentences.zh: 嵐州刺史譚元澄嘗有德於晟，後貶死。

translations.literal: Tan Yuancheng, prefect of Lanzhou, had once shown kindness to Sheng and later was demoted and died.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Yuancheng, prefect of Lan, had once done Sheng a kindness and was later demoted and died in exile.

sentences.zh: 晟既貴，直其枉，詔贈元澄甯州刺史，晟撫其二子，為成就之。

translations.literal: Once Sheng was exalted he set right the injustice; an edict posthumously enfeoffed Yuancheng as prefect of Ningzhou, and Sheng nurtured his two sons and brought them to success.
translations.idiomatic: After Sheng rose high he cleared Tan's name; the court posthumously made Yuancheng prefect of Ning, and Sheng raised his two sons and saw them established in the world.

sentences.zh: 在鳳翔，嘗曰：「魏征以直言致太宗於堯舜上，忠臣也。

translations.literal: At Fengxiang he once said, "Wei Zheng by straight speech raised Taizong to the level of Yao and Shun—a loyal minister.
translations.idiomatic: At Fengxiang he once remarked, "Wei Zheng spoke plainly and lifted Taizong to the level of Yao and Shun—that is a true minister.

sentences.zh: 我誠慕焉。」

translations.literal: I truly admire that."
translations.idiomatic: I sincerely mean to follow his example."

sentences.zh: 行軍司馬李叔度曰：「彼縉紳儒者事，公勳德何希是哉？」

translations.literal: Campaigning staff major Li Shudu said, "That is the affair of gentry scholars; with your merit and virtue why aspire to it?"
translations.idiomatic: His campaigning staff major Li Shudu said, "That is scholars' talk at court—what need has a man of your deeds to envy it?"

sentences.zh: 晟曰：「君失辭。

translations.literal: Sheng said, "You misspeak.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng replied, "You are wrong to say that.

sentences.zh: 晟幸得備將相，苟容身不言，豈可謂有犯無隱邪？
