translations.literal: Sheng has fortunately attained the rank of general and minister; if I merely preserve myself and do not speak, how can that be called having offense yet not concealing it?
translations.idiomatic: I have been lucky enough to stand among generals and ministers; if I kept silent merely to save myself, could I be said to remonstrate without hiding anything?

sentences.zh: 是非唯上所擇爾。」

translations.literal: Right and wrong are for the sovereign alone to choose."
translations.idiomatic: Whether I am right or wrong is for the emperor alone to decide."

sentences.zh: 叔度慚。

translations.literal: Shudu was ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Shudu withdrew in shame.

sentences.zh: 故晟每進對，謇謇盡大臣節，未嘗露於外。

translations.literal: Therefore whenever Sheng advanced in audience he remonstrated earnestly and fully fulfilled a great minister's duty, yet never exposed it outwardly.
translations.idiomatic: Hence in every audience Sheng spoke his mind as a great minister should, yet never paraded his loyalty in public.

sentences.zh: 治家以嚴，子侄非晨昏不輒見，所與言未嘗及公事。

translations.literal: He governed the household with severity; sons and nephews he did not see except morning and evening, and what he spoke with them never touched public affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His household he ran with iron discipline: nephews and sons he saw only at morning and evening greetings, and never discussed state business with them.

sentences.zh: 正歲，崔氏女歸寧，讓曰：「爾有家，而姑在堂，婦當治酒食，且以待賓客。」

translations.literal: On New Year's Day a daughter of the Cui clan came home to visit her parents; he reproved her, saying, "You have a household, yet your mother-in-law is in the hall—a wife ought to prepare food and drink and moreover receive guests."
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day a daughter-in-law of the Cui family came to visit her parents; he rebuked her: "You have a home of your own and your husband's mother is still alive—you should be preparing the feast and receiving guests, not here."

sentences.zh: 即卻之，不得進。

translations.literal: He at once sent her back and would not let her enter.
translations.idiomatic: He turned her away at once and would not let her in.

sentences.zh: 達禮敦教類若此。

translations.literal: In penetrating ritual and promoting instruction he was of this sort throughout.
translations.idiomatic: In observing ritual and teaching his kin he was always like this.

sentences.zh: 與馬燧皆在朝，每宴樂恩賜，使者相銜于道。

translations.literal: He and Ma Sui were both at court; whenever banquets, music, or gracious gifts were granted, envoys followed one another along the road.
translations.idiomatic: He and Ma Sui were both at court, and whenever the throne sent feasts, music, or gifts, couriers lined the road between their mansions.

sentences.zh: 兩家日出無鐘鼓聲，則金吾以聞，少選，使者至，必曰：「今日何不舉樂？」

translations.literal: If by daybreak neither household had the sound of bells and drums, the Golden Guard would report it; shortly an envoy would arrive and invariably say, "Why is there no music today?"
translations.idiomatic: If either house failed to strike bells and drums at dawn, the Golden Guard reported it—and soon a palace messenger would arrive asking, "Why no music today?"

sentences.zh: 既薨，城鹽州，復故池，以新鹽賜宰相。

translations.literal: After his death the city of Yanchzhou was built, the old salt pools were restored, and the new salt was bestowed on the chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: After his death the court fortified Yanchzhou, reopened the old salt pans, and sent the first new salt to the chancellors.

sentences.zh: 帝思晟，乃致鹽靈座。

translations.literal: The emperor, thinking of Sheng, then placed the salt before his spirit seat.
translations.idiomatic: Missing Sheng, the emperor set the salt before his spirit tablet instead.

sentences.zh: 其眷遇終始，無與比者。

translations.literal: His favor from beginning to end had none with whom to compare.
translations.idiomatic: From first to last no subject ever enjoyed such unbroken favor.

sentences.zh: 有十五子，其聞者願、憲、愬、聽雲。

translations.literal: He had fifteen sons; those who became known were Yuan, Xian, Su, and Ting.
translations.idiomatic: He had fifteen sons; those who won renown were Yuan, Xian, Su, and Ting.

sentences.zh: 子 愿 憲

translations.literal: Sons: Yuan and Xian
translations.idiomatic: Sons: Yuan and Xian

sentences.zh: 願少謙謹。

translations.literal: Yuan from youth was modest and cautious.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was modest and careful from boyhood.

sentences.zh: 晟立功時，諸子未官，宰相以聞，即日召授太子賓客、上柱國。

translations.literal: When Sheng achieved merit his sons were not yet in office; the chancellor reported it, and the same day they were summoned and appointed Guests of the Heir Apparent and Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: When Sheng won his great victory his sons held no posts; the chancellor informed the throne, and that same day Yuan was summoned and made a guest of the crown prince and Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 故事，柱國門列戟，遂父子皆賜。

translations.literal: By precedent a Pillar of State's gate displayed halberds, and so father and sons were all granted them.
translations.idiomatic: By custom a Pillar of State might set halberds at his gate, and father and son received the honor alike.

sentences.zh: 元和初，領夏綏銀宥節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe he headed the military commission of Xia, Sui, Yin, and You.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanhe reign he became military governor of Xia, Sui, Yin, and You.

sentences.zh: 政簡而嚴。

translations.literal: His government was simple yet strict.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was spare and stern.

sentences.zh: 部有失馬者，願署牒於道，以金購之。

translations.literal: When someone in the command lost a horse, Yuan posted a notice on the road offering gold to buy it back.
translations.idiomatic: When a trooper lost a horse, Yuan posted a notice along the roads offering gold for its return.

sentences.zh: 三日，失馬並良馬一系署下，且曰：「逸而至，不告，罪當死，謹以良馬贖。」

translations.literal: Within three days the lost horse came, together with a fine horse tied beneath the notice, with a message saying, "It strayed and arrived; for not reporting it the crime deserves death—I respectfully offer a fine horse in ransom."
translations.idiomatic: Within three days the missing horse appeared, with a fine mount tied beneath the notice and a note: "The animal wandered here; not reporting it is a capital offense—I offer this good horse in atonement."

sentences.zh: 願歸失馬，而縱其良，境內肅然。

translations.literal: Yuan returned the lost horse and released the fine one; within the borders all was orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan returned the lost horse and let the donor keep the fine mount; from that day the circuit was orderly.

sentences.zh: 徙節武寧軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to command the Wuning Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to command the Wuning army.

sentences.zh: 會伐青、鄆，數有功，以久疾，用愬代之。

translations.literal: When they campaigned against Qing and Yan he achieved merit several times; because of long illness Su was used to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Qing and Yan he won repeated credit, but chronic illness forced his relief by Li Su.

sentences.zh: 召為刑部尚書，俄檢校尚書左僕射，節度鳳翔，自是邇聲色而政衰矣。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Minister of Justice; soon made acting Vice Director of the Left Secretariat and military commissioner of Fengxiang—from then he drew near to music and women and his government declined.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as minister of justice, he was soon made acting vice director of the left secretariat and military governor of Fengxiang; from then on he gave himself to pleasure and his rule decayed.

sentences.zh: 長慶中，徙宣武。

translations.literal: In the Changqing era he was transferred to Xuanwu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Changqing reign he was moved to Xuanwu.

sentences.zh: 始，張弘靖給其軍頗厚；

translations.literal: At first Zhang Hongjing had supplied his army quite generously;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hongjing had once paid the troops handsomely;

sentences.zh: 願至，府庫殫匱，賞賚不及弘靖時，而侈費過之。

translations.literal: when Yuan arrived the treasury was exhausted, rewards did not reach Hongjing's level, yet his extravagant spending surpassed it.
translations.idiomatic: but when Yuan arrived the treasury was empty, pay fell short of Hongjing's standard, and his personal extravagance exceeded it.

sentences.zh: 以威刑操下，用婚家竇緩典帳中兵，驕驁怠遝。

translations.literal: He controlled subordinates with stern punishment and used his in-law Dou Huan to command the central headquarters troops, who were arrogant, unruly, and slack.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled by terror, put his in-law Dou Huan in charge of headquarters troops, and they grew arrogant and slack.

sentences.zh: 牙將李臣則等因眾不忍，夜斬緩首。

translations.literal: Garrison officer Li Chenze and others, because the troops could not bear it, by night beheaded Huan.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison officer Li Chenze and others, unable to endure the abuse, cut off Huan's head one night.

sentences.zh: 願聞變，不及巾，與左右數人縋而逸，奪野人乘，馳以免。

translations.literal: Yuan heard of the mutiny and, not even tying his headcloth, with a few attendants let himself down by rope and fled, seizing a countryman's cart and galloping to escape.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan heard the uproar and fled without even tying his cap, lowering himself by rope with a few aides, commandeering a peasant cart, and riding for his life.

sentences.zh: 其家死於兵，三子匿而免。

translations.literal: His household perished at the soldiers' hands; three sons hid and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: His family was killed in the violence; three sons hid and survived.

sentences.zh: 兵既亂，因大掠，推李朅主後務，請諸朝。

translations.literal: Once the troops were in disorder they plundered on a great scale, pushed Li Qie to manage subsequent affairs, and requested appointment from the court.
translations.idiomatic: The mutineers looted the city, set up Li Qie to run affairs, and asked the court to confirm him.

sentences.zh: 時責願不職，貶隋州刺史。

translations.literal: At the time Yuan was blamed for dereliction of duty and demoted to prefect of Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The court blamed Yuan for dereliction and demoted him to prefect of Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 入為左金吾衛大將軍，復拜河中、晉、絳等節度使。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as great general of the Left Golden Guard and was again appointed military commissioner of Hezhong, Jin, and Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as general of the Left Golden Guard and again made military governor of Hezhong, Jin, and Jiang.

sentences.zh: 雖嘗以荒侈敗，不能自悛，軍政愈弛，結納權近，官貲隨賂遺輒盡。

translations.literal: Although he had once failed through profligacy and could not reform himself, military government grew ever laxer; he cultivated the powerful at court, and official wealth was spent as soon as bribes came in.
translations.idiomatic: Though his excess had once ruined him, he would not mend his ways; discipline slackened, he courted the powerful, and every official penny vanished into graft.

sentences.zh: 蒲人怨，且亂。

translations.literal: The people of Pu were resentful and near rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Pu seethed with resentment and were on the brink of revolt.

sentences.zh: 會卒，贈司徒。

translations.literal: He happened to die in office and was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office and was posthumously made Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 憲與愬于諸子號最仁孝。

translations.literal: Xian and Su among the sons were called the most filial and dutiful.
translations.idiomatic: Xian and Su were considered the most filial of the sons.

sentences.zh: 長喜儒，以禮法自矜制。

translations.literal: From youth he loved Confucian learning and restrained himself with ritual and law.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved the classics and held himself to ritual and law.

sentences.zh: 調太原府參軍事、醴泉尉。

translations.literal: He was selected as adjutant of Taiyuan prefecture and magistrate of Liquan.
translations.idiomatic: He served as adjutant in Taiyuan prefecture and as magistrate of Liquan.

sentences.zh: 於頔鎮襄陽，辟署於府。

translations.literal: When Yu Di governed Xiangyang he recruited Xian to his staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Di held Xiangyang he took Xian onto his staff.

sentences.zh: 時吳少誠張淮西，獨憚頔威強，時謂憲為之助。

translations.literal: At the time Wu Shaocheng dominated the Huai West; he alone feared Yu Di's might, and the age said Xian was his help.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shaocheng then lorded it over the Huai West and feared only Yu Di's strength; men said Xian was the sword behind it.

sentences.zh: 又辟魏博田弘正幕府，遷衛州刺史，以治行稱。

translations.literal: He was again recruited to Tian Hongzheng's staff in Weibo, promoted to prefect of Weizhou, and was known for the conduct of his government.
translations.idiomatic: He later joined Tian Hongzheng's staff in Weibo, became prefect of Wei, and won praise for good administration.

sentences.zh: 徙絳州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Jiang.

sentences.zh: 絳有幻人訹民以亂，憲執誅之。

translations.literal: In Jiang there was an illusionist who incited the people to disorder; Xian seized and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: A sorcerer in Jiang stirred the people to revolt; Xian arrested and executed him.

sentences.zh: 河中兵本仰食於絳，而汾可輸河、渭，歲租與糴常數十萬石，故敖保山為固，民之輸者，十牛不勝一車。

translations.literal: The troops of Hezhong originally depended on food from Jiang, while Fen could be shipped to the Yellow and Wei rivers; yearly tax grain and purchases regularly ran to several hundred thousand piculs, so Ao Hill was fortified as a stronghold, and for the people who delivered grain ten oxen could not match one cart.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhong's army lived on Jiang's grain, yet grain from across the Fen could reach the Yellow and Wei; yearly tax and purchases totaled hundreds of thousands of piculs. Ao Hill was fortified as a depot, and peasants hauling tribute needed ten ox teams where one cart would do.

sentences.zh: 憲濱汾相地治新倉，當費二百萬，請留垣縣粟糶河南，以錢還糴絳粟，既免負載勞，又權其贏以完新倉，絳人賴利。

translations.literal: Xian along the Fen surveyed the ground and built a new granary, which should cost two million cash; he requested to retain Yuan County grain and sell it in Henan, using the money to buy back Jiang grain—thus avoiding the labor of carrying loads and also using the surplus to complete the new granary; the people of Jiang relied on the benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Xian built a new riverside granary that would cost two million cash. He sold Yuan county's surplus grain in Henan, used the proceeds to buy grain for Jiang, spared the people the back-breaking haul over Ao Hill, and applied the profit to finish the warehouse. Jiang benefited greatly.

sentences.zh: 入為宗正少卿，副金吾大將軍胡證為送太和公主使。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as vice director of the Court of the Imperial Clan and, as deputy to Golden Guard great general Hu Zheng, served as envoy escorting Princess Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: He became vice director of the imperial clan court and, as deputy to Hu Zheng, general of the Golden Guard, escorted Princess Taihe on her mission.

sentences.zh: 還，獻《回鶻道裏記》，遷太府卿。

translations.literal: On return he presented the Record of Roads to the Uyghurs and was promoted to Grand Steward.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he submitted a Record of the Road to the Uyghurs and was made grand steward of the imperial household.

sentences.zh: 太和初，繇江西觀察使遷嶺南節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe he moved from Jiangxi observation commissioner to Lingnan military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taihe reign he rose from Jiangxi observer to military governor of Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 憲，勳伐家子，所曆皆以吏能顯，政績暴著。

translations.literal: Xian, a son of a house of martial achievement, in every post he held displayed administrative ability and his governmental achievements were conspicuous.
translations.idiomatic: Xian, born to a house of martial glory, distinguished himself everywhere by administrative talent, and his record was brilliant.

sentences.zh: 善治律令，性明恕，詳正大獄，活無罪者數百人。

translations.literal: He was skilled in governing by statutes and ordinances, by nature clear and forgiving; in examining and judging great cases he spared several hundred who were without guilt.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the law codes, was clear-minded and merciful, and in major trials saved hundreds of innocent men.

sentences.zh: 卒官下。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 子 愬

translations.literal: Son: Su
translations.idiomatic: Son: Su

sentences.zh: 憲宗討吳元濟，唐鄧節度使高霞寓既敗，以袁滋代將，復無功。

translations.literal: When Xianzong campaigned against Wu Yuanji, Tang-Deng military commissioner Gao Xiayu having already been defeated, Yuan Zi was used to replace him as commander, yet again without achievement.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzong attacked Wu Yuanji, Gao Xiayu, military governor of Tang and Deng, was beaten; Yuan Zi replaced him and failed again.

sentences.zh: 愬求自試，宰相李逢吉亦以愬可用，遂檢校左散騎常侍，為隋唐鄧節度使。

translations.literal: Su requested to try himself; Chancellor Li Fengji also held Su usable, and so he was made acting Left Regular Attendant and military commissioner of Sui, Tang, and Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Su volunteered for command; Chancellor Li Fengji backed him, and he was made acting left regular attendant and military governor of Sui, Tang, and Deng.

sentences.zh: 愬以其軍初傷夷，士氣未完，乃不為斥候部伍。

translations.literal: Su, because his army had at first suffered wounds and morale was not yet complete, therefore did not set out scouts or arrange ranks.
translations.idiomatic: His army was still battered and morale fragile, so Su posted no scouts and kept no battle order.

sentences.zh: 或有言者，愬曰：「賊方安袁公之寬，吾不欲使震而備我。」

translations.literal: When some spoke of it Su said, "The rebels are just now at ease with Lord Yuan's leniency; I do not wish to alarm them so they prepare against me."
translations.idiomatic: When aides objected he said, "The enemy is still comfortable with Yuan's easy ways—I do not want to startle them into guarding against me."

sentences.zh: 乃令於軍曰：「天子知愬能忍恥，故委以撫養。

translations.literal: He then ordered in the army, "The Son of Heaven knows Su can bear shame, and therefore entrusted him with nurturing and care.
translations.idiomatic: He told the troops, "The emperor knows I can swallow insult, and that is why he sent me to nurse you back to health.

sentences.zh: 戰，非吾事也。」

translations.literal: Fighting is not my affair."
translations.idiomatic: Fighting is not my business."

sentences.zh: 眾信而安之。

translations.literal: The masses believed and were at ease.
translations.idiomatic: The men believed him and settled down.

sentences.zh: 乃斥倡優，未嘗嬉樂。

translations.literal: He then dismissed singers and actors and never indulged in merrymaking.
translations.idiomatic: He dismissed entertainers and never joined in revelry.

sentences.zh: 士傷夷病疾，親為營護。

translations.literal: When soldiers were wounded or ill he personally tended and cared for them.
translations.idiomatic: When men were wounded or sick he nursed them himself.

sentences.zh: 蔡人以嘗敗辱霞寓等，又愬名非夙所畏者，易之，不為備。

translations.literal: The Cai people, because they had once defeated and shamed Xiayu and the rest, and moreover Su's name was not one they had long feared, took him lightly and did not prepare.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels of Cai, having already humiliated Gao Xiayu and his predecessors, and never having feared Li Su's name, despised him and took no precautions.

sentences.zh: 愬沈鷙，務推誠待士，故能張其卑弱而用之。

translations.literal: Su was deep and stern, striving to treat soldiers with pushed-forward sincerity, and therefore could extend their low weakness and use them.
translations.idiomatic: Su was reserved and shrewd, yet he dealt with his men in open sincerity and so could stretch their battered weakness into strength.

sentences.zh: 賊來降，輒聽其便，或父母與孤未葬者，給粟帛遣還，勞之曰：「而亦王人也，無棄親戚。」

translations.literal: When rebels came to surrender he always let them go as they wished; if parents or orphans were still unburied he gave grain and silk and sent them back, encouraging them, "You too are the king's people—do not abandon your kin."
translations.idiomatic: When defectors came he let them go as they pleased; if parents or kin lay unburied he gave grain and cloth and sent them home, saying, "You are the emperor's subjects too—do not desert your families."

sentences.zh: 眾願為愬死，故山川險易與賊情偽，一能曉之。

translations.literal: The masses were willing to die for Su; therefore of mountain and river, difficult and easy, and the rebels' conditions true and false, he understood them all.
translations.idiomatic: His men would have died for him, and he came to know every path, every trick, and every secret of the enemy camp.

sentences.zh: 居半歲，知士可用，乃請濟師；

translations.literal: After half a year he knew the soldiers could be used and then requested reinforcing troops;
translations.idiomatic: After six months he knew the army was ready and asked for reinforcements;

sentences.zh: 詔益河中、鄜坊二千騎。

translations.literal: an edict added two thousand cavalry from Hezhong and Bin-Fang.
translations.idiomatic: the court added two thousand horse from Hezhong and Bin-Fang.

sentences.zh: 於是繕鎧厲兵，攻馬鞍山，下之；

translations.literal: Thereupon he repaired armor and sharpened weapons, attacked Mount Ma, and took it;
translations.idiomatic: He then readied armor and honed weapons, stormed Mount Ma, and captured it.

sentences.zh: 拔道口柵，戰嵖岈山，以取爐冶城；

translations.literal: He stormed Daokou stockade, fought at Mount Chaya, and thereby seized Furnace-Foundry City;
translations.idiomatic: He carried Daokou stockade, fought at Mount Chaya, and won Furnace-Foundry City.

sentences.zh: 入白狗、汶港柵，披楚城，襲朗山，再執守將。

translations.literal: He entered the White Dog and Wen Harbor stockades, broke through Chu city, raided Langshan, and again seized the garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed through the White Dog and Wen Harbor palisades, overran Chu city, struck Langshan, and twice took the defending generals prisoner.

sentences.zh: 平青陵城，禽驍將丁士良，異其才，不殺，署捉生將。

translations.literal: He pacified Qingling city, captured fierce general Ding Shiliang, marveled at his talent, did not kill him, and appointed him captive officer.
translations.idiomatic: He reduced Qingling city, captured the fearsome general Ding Shiliang, admired his ability, spared his life, and made him a live-capture officer.

sentences.zh: 士良謝曰：「吳秀琳以數千兵不可破者，陳光洽為之謀也。

translations.literal: Shiliang thanked him, saying, "Wu Xiulin's several thousand troops cannot be broken because Chen Guangye plans for him.
translations.idiomatic: Shiliang thanked him and said, "The reason Wu Xiulin's thousands seem unbreakable is that Chen Guangye advises him.

sentences.zh: 我能為公取之。」

translations.literal: I can take him for you."
translations.idiomatic: I can capture him for you.

sentences.zh: 乃禽以獻。

translations.literal: Thereupon he captured Guangye and presented him.
translations.idiomatic: He did so and presented Guangye as his prize.

sentences.zh: 於是秀琳舉文城柵降。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xiulin surrendered Wencheng stockade entire.
translations.idiomatic: Xiulin then surrendered the Wencheng palisade.

sentences.zh: 遂以其眾攻吳房，殘外垣。

translations.literal: He then used his troops to attack Wufang and wrecked the outer wall.
translations.idiomatic: He next led those forces against Wufang and battered its outer ramparts.

sentences.zh: 始出攻，吏曰：「往亡日，法當避。」

translations.literal: When he was first setting out to attack, an official said, "It is a 'going-forth-void' day; by rule one should avoid it."
translations.idiomatic: As he prepared to march, an officer said, "Today is an ill-omened day for campaigning—the law says we should hold back.

sentences.zh: 愬曰：「彼謂吾不來，此可擊也。」

translations.literal: Su said, "They think we will not come—this is the moment to strike."
translations.idiomatic: Li Su replied, "They believe we will not come—that is exactly when we should strike."

sentences.zh: 既引還，賊以精騎尾擊。

translations.literal: Having already drawn back, the rebels pursued with elite cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: On the withdrawal, rebel elite horse harried his rear.

sentences.zh: 愬下馬據胡床，令軍曰：「退者斬。」

translations.literal: Su dismounted and sat on a folding camp chair, ordering the army, "Whoever retreats—beheaded."
translations.idiomatic: Su dismounted and planted himself on a camp stool, shouting, "Anyone who falls back dies.

sentences.zh: 眾決死戰，射殺其將，賊乃走。

translations.literal: The masses fought resolved to die, shot and killed their general, and the rebels then fled.
translations.idiomatic: The men fought as if death meant nothing, killed an enemy commander with arrows, and the rebels broke.

sentences.zh: 或勸遂取吳房，愬曰：「不可。

translations.literal: Some urged him then to take Wufang; Su said, "It cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged him to seize Wufang at once; Su said, "No.

sentences.zh: 吳房拔，則賊力專，不若留之以分其力。」

translations.literal: If Wufang is taken, then the rebels' strength is concentrated; better to leave it and divide their strength."
translations.idiomatic: If we take Wufang, their strength gathers in one place; better leave it and keep them divided."

sentences.zh: 初，秀琳降，愬單騎抵柵下與語，親釋縛，署以為將。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Xiulin surrendered, Su rode alone to the foot of the stockade to speak with him, personally untied his bonds, and appointed him a general.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiulin first submitted, Su rode alone to the palisade, spoke with him face to face, cut his bonds himself, and made him a general.

sentences.zh: 秀琳為愬策曰：「必破賊，非李祐無與成功者。」

translations.literal: Xiulin counseled Su, saying, "To be sure to break the rebels, apart from Li You none shares in success."
translations.idiomatic: Xiulin advised him: "You will not break them without Li You—no one else can do it.

sentences.zh: 祐，賊健將也，守興橋柵，其戰嘗易官軍。

translations.literal: You was the rebels' stalwart general, holding Xingqiao stockade; in battle he had often rolled back government troops.
translations.idiomatic: You was their toughest commander, holding Xingqiao stockade, and had repeatedly routed imperial forces.

sentences.zh: 愬候祐護獲於野，遣史用誠以壯騎三百伏其旁，見羸卒若將燔聚者，祐果輕出，用誠禽而還。

translations.literal: Su waited until You was out guarding booty in the fields, sent Shi Yongcheng with three hundred stout horsemen lying in ambush beside him; seeing weak soldiers as if about to burn a camp, You truly came out lightly; Yongcheng captured him and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Su watched until You was out foraging in the field, then sent Shi Yongcheng with three hundred picked cavalry to lie in wait. When You saw what looked like a small party about to burn supplies, he rode out carelessly—and Yongcheng seized him and brought him in.

sentences.zh: 諸將素苦祐，請殺之，愬不聽，以為客。

translations.literal: The generals had long suffered from You and asked to kill him; Su would not listen and treated him as a guest.
translations.idiomatic: The other commanders, who had long hated You, begged for his head; Su refused and received him as an honored guest.

sentences.zh: 待間，召祐及李忠義屏人語，至夜艾。

translations.literal: Waiting for leisure, he summoned You and Li Zhongyi, dismissed others, and spoke until deep night.
translations.idiomatic: At the first quiet hour he called You and Li Zhongyi aside and talked with them until deep night.

sentences.zh: 忠義，亦賊將，所謂李憲者。

translations.literal: Zhongyi was also a rebel general—the one called Li Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyi was another rebel commander, known also as Li Xian.

sentences.zh: 軍中多諫此二人不可近，愬待益厚。

translations.literal: Many in the army admonished that these two must not be approached; Su treated them all the more generously.
translations.idiomatic: Many in camp warned him to keep his distance from the pair; Su drew them closer still.

sentences.zh: 乃募死士三千人為突將，自教之。

translations.literal: He then recruited three thousand death-defying men as shock troops and personally drilled them.
translations.idiomatic: He raised three thousand volunteers for a shock corps and trained them himself.

sentences.zh: 會雨，自五月至七月不止，軍中以為不殺祐之罰，將吏雜然不解。

translations.literal: It happened to rain; from the fifth month to the seventh it did not stop; the army took it as punishment for not killing You; officers and clerks were in mixed uproar, uncomprehending.
translations.idiomatic: Rain fell without cease from the fifth month through the seventh. The troops took it as heaven's punishment for sparing You, and officers grumbled in open confusion.

sentences.zh: 愬力不能獨完祐，乃持以泣曰：「天不欲平賊乎？

translations.literal: Su's strength could not alone preserve You intact; he then took him in his embrace weeping, saying, "Does Heaven not wish the rebels pacified?
translations.idiomatic: Unable to shield You alone, Su clasped him and wept: "Does Heaven refuse us victory over these rebels?

sentences.zh: 何見奪者眾邪？」

translations.literal: Why are those who seize him so many?"
translations.idiomatic: Why do so many demand his life?

sentences.zh: 則械而送之朝，表言必殺祐，無與共誅蔡者。

translations.literal: Then he put him in fetters and sent him to court, memorializing that You must be killed and none shared in joint punishment of Cai.
translations.idiomatic: He had You bound and sent to the capital with a memorial insisting that killing You would doom any hope of taking Cai.

sentences.zh: 詔釋以還愬。

translations.literal: An edict released him and returned him to Su.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered him freed and sent back to Su.

sentences.zh: 愬乃令佩刀出入帳下，署六院兵馬使。

translations.literal: Su then ordered him to wear a sword in coming and going below the tent, appointing him horse-and-foot marshal of the Six Courts.
translations.idiomatic: Su let him wear a sword at his side day and night and made him marshal of the Six Courts hosts.

sentences.zh: 六院者，隋、唐兵也，凡三千人，皆山南奇材銳士，故委祐統之。

translations.literal: The Six Courts were Sui and Tang troops—altogether three thousand, all extraordinary talent and sharp warriors of Shannan; therefore he entrusted You to command them.
translations.idiomatic: The Six Courts were the old Sui–Tang corps—three thousand of Shannan's finest blades—and Su placed them entirely under You's command.

sentences.zh: 祐捧檄嗚咽，諸將乃不敢言，由是始定襲蔡之謀矣。

translations.literal: You received the commission in sobbing, the generals then dared not speak; from this the plan to strike Cai was first settled.
translations.idiomatic: You took the commission with tears; the other generals fell silent; and the night assault on Cai was at last decided.

sentences.zh: 舊令，敢舍諜者族。

translations.literal: An old order: whoever dared harbor spies—clan extermination.
translations.idiomatic: Old regulations condemned to clan extinction anyone who sheltered enemy spies.

sentences.zh: 愬刊其令，一切撫之，故諜者反效以情，愬益悉賊虛實。

translations.literal: Su struck out that order and in every case comforted them; therefore spies in turn reported intelligence, and Su all the more thoroughly knew the rebels' void and fullness.
translations.idiomatic: Su repealed that rule and treated every turncoat kindly, so enemy agents began reporting back to him—and he learned the rebels' strengths and weaknesses in full.

sentences.zh: 時李光顏戰數勝，元濟悉銳卒屯洄曲以抗光顏。

translations.literal: At this time Li Guangyan fought and repeatedly won; Yuanji massed all crack troops at Huaiqu to oppose Guangyan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangyan was winning battle after battle; Wu Yuanji massed his best troops at Huaiqu to hold him.

sentences.zh: 愬知其隙可乘，乃遣從事鄭澥見裴度告師期，于時元和十一年十月己卯。

translations.literal: Su knew the gap could be exploited; he then sent staff officer Zheng Xie to see Pei Du and report the campaign date—at that time the jimao day of the tenth month of the eleventh year of Yuanhe.
translations.idiomatic: Su saw his opening and sent staff officer Zheng Xie to Pei Du with the battle date: the jimao day of the tenth month, Yuanhe year eleven.

sentences.zh: 師夜起，祐以突將三千為前鋒，李忠義副之，愬率中軍三千，田進誠以下軍殿。

translations.literal: The army rose at night; You led three thousand shock troops as vanguard with Li Zhongyi as second, Su led three thousand in the center army, Tian Jincheng brought up the rear with the lower army.
translations.idiomatic: The column marched at night: You led three thousand shock troops in the van with Li Zhongyi beside him, Su commanded three thousand in the center, and Tian Jincheng's division formed the rear guard.

sentences.zh: 出文城柵，令曰：「引而東。」

translations.literal: Departing Wencheng stockade, the order ran: "Lead and go east."
translations.idiomatic: Leaving Wencheng palisade, he ordered, "March east.

sentences.zh: 六十里止，襲張柴，殲其戍。

translations.literal: After sixty li they halted, struck Zhangchai, and annihilated its garrison.
translations.idiomatic: They halted sixty li out, surprised Zhangchai, and wiped out its garrison.

sentences.zh: 敕士少休，益治鞍鎧，發刃彀弓。

translations.literal: He commanded the soldiers to rest briefly, all the more to tend saddles and armor, to draw blades and bend bows.
translations.idiomatic: He let the men breathe, tightened tack and armor, and drew every blade and bow.

sentences.zh: 會大雨雪，天晦，凜風偃旗裂膚，馬皆縮栗，士抱戈凍死於道十一二。

translations.literal: It happened to be great rain and snow; heaven was dark; biting wind bent flags and split the skin; horses all shrank and shivered; soldiers hugging spears froze dead on the road—one or two in ten.
translations.idiomatic: A blizzard came on. The sky went black. Wind bit through banners and flesh alike. Horses trembled; one man in ten froze stiff still clutching his weapon on the march.

sentences.zh: 張柴之東，陂澤阻奧，眾未嘗蹈也，皆謂投不測。

translations.literal: East of Zhangchai were marshes and swamps, blocked and deep—the masses had never trod there; all said they were cast into the unknowable.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond Zhangchai lay bog and fen none of them had ever crossed; many believed they were marching into the unknown.

sentences.zh: 始發，吏請所向，愬曰：「入蔡州取吳元濟！」

translations.literal: When first setting out, an official asked the destination; Su said, "Enter Cai Prefecture and take Wu Yuanji!"
translations.idiomatic: As they set out, an officer asked their objective. Su said, "We are marching on Cai Prefecture to seize Wu Yuanji!

sentences.zh: 士失色，監軍使者泣曰：「果落祐計。」

translations.literal: The soldiers' faces lost color; the army monitor envoy wept, saying, "We have truly fallen into You's plot.
translations.idiomatic: The men went pale. The monitor envoy burst into tears: "We have walked straight into You's trap."

sentences.zh: 然業從愬，人人不敢自為計。

translations.literal: Yet already committed to following Su, each man dared not make his own plan.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they were already committed to following Su, and none dared speak for himself.

sentences.zh: 愬道分輕兵斷橋以絕洄曲道，又以兵絕朗山道。

translations.literal: On the road Su divided light troops to break bridges and cut off the Huaiqu route, and again with troops cut off the Langshan route.
translations.idiomatic: Along the way Su sent light detachments to destroy bridges and sever the Huaiqu road, and posted men to block the Langshan route as well.

sentences.zh: 行七十里，夜半至懸瓠城，雪甚，城旁皆鵝鶩池，愬令擊之，以亂軍聲。

translations.literal: Marching seventy li, at midnight they reached Xuanhuo city; snow was heavy; beside the walls were all goose and duck ponds—Su ordered them struck to confuse army sounds.
translations.idiomatic: After seventy li they reached the walls at midnight. Snow lay deep; goose and duck ponds ringed the city. Su had his men beat the water to mask the noise of the assault.

sentences.zh: 賊恃吳房、朗山戍，晏然無知者。

translations.literal: The rebels relied on the Wufang and Langshan garrisons and were placidly without any who knew.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels, trusting their outposts at Wufang and Langshan, suspected nothing.

sentences.zh: 祐等坎墉先登，眾從之，殺門者，發關，留持柝傳夜自如。

translations.literal: You and the rest breached the rampart first and ascended; the masses followed; they killed the gate guards, threw open the pass, and left men holding clappers to sound the night watches as usual.
translations.idiomatic: You broke the wall and climbed first; the rest poured after. They killed the gate guards, threw open the bar, and left men to beat the night watch as if nothing had changed.

sentences.zh: 黎明，雪止，愬入駐元濟外宅。

translations.literal: At dawn the snow stopped; Su entered and lodged at Yuanji's outer residence.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the snow ceased. Su entered and took up station in Yuanji's outer quarters.

sentences.zh: 蔡吏驚曰：「城陷矣！」

translations.literal: Cai officials cried in alarm, "The city has fallen!"
translations.idiomatic: Cai officials cried, "The city is lost!

sentences.zh: 元濟尚不信，曰：「是洄曲子弟來索褚衣爾。」

translations.literal: Yuanji still did not believe, saying, "It is the Huaiqu lads come demanding padded garments—that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yuanji still would not believe it. "Those are just the Huaiqu troops come for winter clothes," he said.

sentences.zh: 及聞號令曰：「常侍傳語。」

translations.literal: When he heard the command cry, "The Regular Attendant sends word,"
translations.idiomatic: Then he heard the call: "A message from the Regular Attendant."

sentences.zh: 始驚曰：「何常侍得在此！」

translations.literal: he then started in alarm, saying, "How does the Regular Attendant come to be here!"
translations.idiomatic: Only then did he start in horror: "How can the Regular Attendant be here?"

sentences.zh: 率左右登牙城，田進誠兵薄之。

translations.literal: Leading his close attendants he ascended the parapet city; Tian Jincheng's troops pressed him close.
translations.idiomatic: He scrambled with his guards onto the inner citadel; Tian Jincheng's men pressed the attack.

sentences.zh: 愬計元濟且望救于董重質，乃訪其家慰安之，使無怖，以書召重質；

translations.literal: Su calculated that Yuanji would soon hope for rescue from Dong Chongzhi; he then visited Chongzhi's family to comfort and reassure them so they would not fear, and with a letter summoned Chongzhi;
translations.idiomatic: Su reckoned Yuanji would look to Dong Chongzhi for relief. He visited Chongzhi's household to calm them, then summoned Chongzhi by letter;

sentences.zh: 重質以單騎白衣降，愬待以禮。

translations.literal: Chongzhi came in single horse and white dress to surrender; Su received him with ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhi came alone, in plain dress, and submitted; Su received him with full courtesy.

sentences.zh: 進誠火南門，元濟請罪，梯而下，檻送京師。

translations.literal: Jincheng fired the south gate; Yuanji asked punishment, came down by ladder, and was sent to the capital in a cage.
translations.idiomatic: Jincheng set fire to the south gate. Yuanji begged mercy, climbed down a ladder, and was sent to the capital in a cage.

sentences.zh: 申、光諸屯尚二萬眾，皆降，愬不戮一人。

translations.literal: The Shen and Guang garrisons and the rest still had twenty thousand; all surrendered; Su slaughtered not a single man.
translations.idiomatic: Some twenty thousand men still held the Shen and Guang posts; all surrendered, and Su killed not one.

sentences.zh: 其為賊執事帳內廚廄廝役，悉用其舊，使不疑。

translations.literal: Those who had served the rebels in offices, within the tents, kitchens, stables, and menial tasks—he all employed them in their old posts, so they would not suspect.
translations.idiomatic: He kept every rebel clerk, cook, groom, and servant in his former post so no one would suspect a trap.

sentences.zh: 乃屯兵鞠場以俟裴度。

translations.literal: He then encamped troops on the drill ground to await Pei Du.
translations.idiomatic: He bivouacked his men on the parade ground to await Pei Du.

sentences.zh: 至，愬以櫜鞬見，度將避之，愬曰：「此方廢上下分久矣，請因示之。」

translations.literal: When Du arrived, Su met him with bared sword-belt and quiver; Du was about to withdraw; Su said, "This place has long since cast off the divide of superior and inferior—please therefore display it."
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Du arrived, Su met him with arms ungirt and bow at his back. Du made to step aside. Su said, "These people have forgotten court discipline for years—show them what obedience looks like.

sentences.zh: 度以宰相禮受愬謁，蔡人聳觀。

translations.literal: Du with chancellor's rites received Su's salutation; the people of Cai craned to watch.
translations.idiomatic: Du accepted Su's salute with full ministerial ceremony while the people of Cai looked on, astonished.

sentences.zh: 乃還屯文城柵。

translations.literal: He then returned to camp at Wencheng stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Su then withdrew his camp to Wencheng palisade.

sentences.zh: 有詔進檢校尚書左僕射、山南東道節度使，封涼國公，實封戶五百，賜一子五品官。

translations.literal: There was an edict promoting him to acting Left Vice Minister of the Secretariat and military governor of Shannan East Circuit, enfeoffing him as Duke of Liang State, with five hundred taxable households in solid fief, and granting one son a fifth-rank office.
translations.idiomatic: An edict promoted him acting Left Vice Minister of the Secretariat and governor of Shannan East, ennobled him Duke of Liang with five hundred taxable households, and granted a fifth-rank post to one of his sons.

sentences.zh: 帝方經略隴右，故徙愬節度鳳翔。

translations.literal: The emperor was then planning the strategy of Longyou; therefore Su was transferred to govern as military commissioner of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was planning operations in Longyou and transferred Su to the Fengxiang command.

sentences.zh: 李師道反，詔愬代願帥武寧軍。

translations.literal: When Li Shidao rebelled, an edict ordered Su to replace Yuan in commanding Wuning Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Shidao rose in rebellion, Su was ordered to replace Li Yuan as commander of the Wuning army.

sentences.zh: 旬日踐父兄兩鎮，世以為榮。

translations.literal: Within ten days he had trodden the two domains of father and elder brother—the age took it as glory.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days he held the same two commands his father and brother had once held—a glory the age thought unmatched.

sentences.zh: 董重質得罪被斥，愬請賜軍中自效，許之，乃署為牙將。

translations.literal: Dong Chongzhi, having offended, was demoted and dismissed; Su requested he be granted to the army to repay with effort; it was approved; he was then appointed a headquarters guard general.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Chongzhi had fallen from favor and been dismissed; Su asked that he be allowed to serve in his army and appointed him a headquarters guard.

sentences.zh: 愬與賊戰金鄉，破之。

translations.literal: Su fought the rebels at Jinxiang and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Su met the enemy at Jinxiang and routed them.

sentences.zh: 凡十一遇，禽其隊帥五十，俘馘萬計。

translations.literal: Altogether in eleven encounters he captured fifty of their squad leaders; captives and severed heads numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In eleven engagements he took fifty enemy captains and counted prisoners and heads in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 淄青平，進同中書門下平章事，徙昭義節度，賜第興寧裏。

translations.literal: When Ziqing was pacified he was advanced to Co-equal-with-the-Department-under-the-Gate Master of Affairs, transferred to Zhaoyi commissioner, and granted a mansion in Xingning Ward.
translations.idiomatic: When Ziqing was pacified he was made co-equal chief minister, transferred to the Zhaoyi command, and given a mansion in Xingning Lane.

sentences.zh: 會田弘正守鎮州，乃以愬帥魏博。

translations.literal: When Tian Hongzheng was defending Zhen Prefecture, Su was then made to command Weibo.
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Hongzheng held Zhenzhou, Su was assigned to command Weibo.

sentences.zh: 長慶初，幽、鎮亂，殺弘正，愬素服以令軍曰：「魏人富庶而通於天化者，田公力也。

translations.literal: Early in Changqing, You and Zhen rebelled and killed Hongzheng; Su in plain white garments issued orders to the army, saying, "The Weibo people's wealth and their communion with Heaven's transforming grace are Tian Gong's power.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Changqing the Yan and Zhen factions rebelled and slew Hongzheng. Su appeared before the army in mourning white and declared: "Whatever prosperity and loyalty the people of Weibo still know, they owe to Lord Tian.

sentences.zh: 上以其愛人，使往治鎮。

translations.literal: The sovereign, because he loved the people, sent him to govern Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor loved this people and sent him to govern Zhen.

sentences.zh: 且田公撫魏七年，今鎮人不道而戕害之，是無魏也。

translations.literal: Moreover Lord Tian had comforted Weibo seven years; now the Zhen people were without the Way and slew and harmed him—this is to have no Weibo.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Tian ruled Weibo seven years, and now men of Zhen have murdered him without cause—as if they meant to wipe Weibo itself from the map.

sentences.zh: 父兄子弟食田公恩者，何以報之？」

translations.literal: Fathers and elder brothers, sons and younger brothers who ate Lord Tian's grace—how will they repay it?"
translations.idiomatic: If you received Lord Tian's kindness—as fathers, sons, brothers—how will you repay it?

sentences.zh: 眾皆哭。

translations.literal: The masses all wept.
translations.idiomatic: The army wept.

sentences.zh: 又以玉帶、寶劍遺牛元翼，曰：「此劍吾先人嘗以揃大盜，吾又以平蔡奸。

translations.literal: He also with jade belt and precious sword sent a gift to Niu Yuanyi, saying, "This sword my forebear once used to smite great bandits; I again used it to pacify Cai's traitors.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Niu Yuanyi a jade belt and treasured sword, saying, "My forebears used this blade against great outlaws; I used it to bring down the Cai rebels.

sentences.zh: 今鎮人逆天，公宜用此夷之也。」

translations.literal: Now the Zhen people oppose Heaven—my lord should use this to level them.
translations.idiomatic: The men of Zhen defy Heaven—take this sword and level them.

sentences.zh: 元翼感動，謝曰：「敢有不承而愛其死力！」

translations.literal: Yuanyi was moved and thanked him, saying, "How would I dare not accept yet spare my utmost strength in death!"
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyi was deeply moved and pledged, "I would never refuse—command me to spend my life!"

sentences.zh: 乃下令軍中，勒兵以俟。

translations.literal: He then issued orders in the army and drilled troops to await.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his army to muster and stand ready.

sentences.zh: 會愬疾甚，不能軍，詔田布代之，以太子少保還東都。

translations.literal: It happened that Su's illness was severe and he could not command the army; an edict had Tian Bu replace him; he returned to the Eastern Capital as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: But Su fell gravely ill and could not take the field. Tian Bu was ordered to replace him, and Su returned to Luoyang as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 卒，年四十九，贈太尉，諡曰武。

translations.literal: He died, age forty-nine; posthumously enfeoffed Grand Preceptor; posthumous title Martial.
translations.idiomatic: He died at forty-nine, was posthumously made Grand Preceptor, and was given the temple name Martial.

sentences.zh: 愬行己儉約。

translations.literal: Su in personal conduct was frugal and restrained.
translations.idiomatic: Li Su lived simply and sparingly.

sentences.zh: 其昆弟賴家勳貴，飾輿馬，矜室廬，唯愬所處乃父時故院，無所增廣。

translations.literal: His brothers relied on the family's merit and nobility, adorning carriages and horses, boasting in halls and cottages—only Su's dwelling was still his father's old courtyard of the time, with nothing added or expanded.
translations.idiomatic: His brothers, riding the family's fame, filled their stables and mansions with ornament; Su alone kept his father's old courtyard, unchanged.

sentences.zh: 始，晟克京師，市不改肆，愬平蔡，亦如之。

translations.literal: In the beginning when Sheng took the capital, the markets did not change their stalls; when Su pacified Cai, it was likewise.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Sheng took Chang'an the markets never closed their stalls; when Li Su pacified Cai, the same held true.

sentences.zh: 功名之奇，近世所未有。

translations.literal: The marvel of his achievement and fame—in recent generations there had been none.
translations.idiomatic: Such achievement was unrivaled in living memory.

sentences.zh: 晚雖忽於取士，與鄭注善，議者不以掩其賢。

translations.literal: In later years though he was heedless in securing scholars and was friendly with Zheng Zhu, commentators did not on that account cover his worth.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he grew careless about recruiting talent and befriended Zheng Zhu, yet critics did not let that obscure his merit.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：愬得李祐不殺，付以兵不疑，知可以破賊也。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Su obtained Li You and did not kill him, entrusted him with troops without doubt—knowing that he could break the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The chroniclers write: Li Su spared Li You, entrusted him with troops without hesitation, knowing he alone could break the enemy.

sentences.zh: 祐受任不辭，決策入死，以愬能用其謀也。

translations.literal: You accepted the commission without declining, resolved on entering death—because Su could employ his plan.
translations.idiomatic: You accepted the charge without demur and marched into mortal peril because Su would use his counsel.

sentences.zh: 祐之才，待愬乃顯，故曰平蔡功，愬為多。

translations.literal: You's talent waited on Su to be displayed; therefore they say in the merit of pacifying Cai, Su's share was the greater.
translations.idiomatic: You's gifts found their field only under Su; thus the glory of pacifying Cai belongs chiefly to Su.

sentences.zh: 子 聽

translations.literal: Son: Ting
translations.idiomatic: His son: Ting

sentences.zh: 聽，字正思，七歲以廕為協律郎，父吏少之，不甚敬，聽輒使鞭之，晟奇其才。

translations.literal: Ting, style Zhengsi, at seven years by yin privilege became Director of Harmonics; when his father's clerks slighted him and did not much respect him, Ting would have them whipped; Sheng marveled at his talent.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ting, style name Zhengsi, became Director of Harmonics at seven by inherited privilege. When his father's clerks looked down on him, he had them flogged—and Li Sheng marveled at his spirit.

sentences.zh: 長乃辟佐於頔府。

translations.literal: When grown he was summoned as aide in Yuan's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he entered service as aide in Li Yuan's command.

sentences.zh: 吐突承璀討王承宗，以聽為神策行營兵馬使。

translations.literal: Tu Gu Chengcui campaigned against Wang Chengzong, appointing Ting as horse-and-foot marshal of the Divine Strategy field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Tu Gu Chengcui marched against Wang Chengzong, he made Ting cavalry commander of the Divine Strategy field army.

sentences.zh: 既戰，斬賊驍將，憲宗壯之，詔圖狀以獻。

translations.literal: After battle he beheaded a fierce rebel general; Emperor Xianzong thought him stalwart and ordered his likeness painted and presented.
translations.idiomatic: In battle he slew a rebel champion. Emperor Xianzong was impressed and ordered his portrait sent to court.

sentences.zh: 承璀數問聽計，卒縛盧從史。

translations.literal: Chengcui repeatedly asked Ting's stratagems and in the end bound Lu Congshi.
translations.idiomatic: Chengcui sought his counsel again and again, and in the end Ting helped capture Lu Congshi.

sentences.zh: 遷左驍衛將軍，出為蔚州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Left Illustrious Cavalry Guard, and went out as prefect of Wei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general of the Left Illustrious Cavalry and sent out as prefect of Wei.

sentences.zh: 州有銅冶，自天寶後廢不治，民盜鑄不禁。

translations.literal: The prefecture had a copper smeltery; since the Tianbao era it had lain abandoned and unrepaired, and the people illicitly cast coin without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture held copper works that had lain idle since the Tianbao years; private casting ran unchecked.

sentences.zh: 聽乃開五爐，官鑄錢日五萬，人無犯者。

translations.literal: Ting then opened five furnaces; the government minted fifty thousand coins a day, and no one violated the law.
translations.idiomatic: Ting reopened five furnaces and had the government mint fifty thousand coins a day; thereafter no one dared cast illicitly.

sentences.zh: 徙安州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to An Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to An prefecture.

sentences.zh: 會觀察使柳公綽方討蔡，以聽典軍，一一咨之，聲振賊中。

translations.literal: It happened that observation commissioner Liu Gongchuo was then campaigning against Cai; he put Ting in command of the army and consulted him on every matter—his fame shook the rebel camp.
translations.idiomatic: When observation commissioner Liu Gongchuo marched against Cai, he gave Ting command of the army and sought his counsel at every turn; Ting's name resounded through the rebel ranks.

sentences.zh: 召為羽林將軍。

translations.literal: He was summoned as General of the Feathered Forest.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as a general of the Feathered Forest Guard.

sentences.zh: 帝討李師道，出聽楚州刺史。

translations.literal: The emperor campaigned against Li Shidao and sent Ting out as prefect of Chu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor marched against Li Shidao, he sent Li Ting out as prefect of Chu.

sentences.zh: 淮西兵綿弱，鄆人素易之。

translations.literal: The Huaixi troops were slack and weak; the men of Yan had always held them in contempt.
translations.idiomatic: Huaixi troops were soft, and the Yan men had long despised them.

sentences.zh: 聽日整勒，士皆奮。

translations.literal: Ting daily drilled and tightened discipline; the soldiers all took heart.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ting drilled them day after day until every man burned to fight.

sentences.zh: 即掩賊不虞，趨漣水，破沭陽，絕龍沮堰，遂取海州，攻朐山，降之，懷仁、東海兩城望風送款。

translations.literal: He at once struck the rebels unawares, hastened to Lianshui, broke Shuyang, cut the Longju weir, then took Haizhou, attacked Qushan and received its surrender; the two cities of Huairen and Donghai submitted at the mere rumor of his approach.
translations.idiomatic: He fell on the enemy by surprise, raced to Lianshui, shattered Shuyang, severed the Longju weir, seized Haizhou, stormed Qushan and took its surrender, and Huairen and Donghai opened their gates at his approach.

sentences.zh: 以功兼御史大夫，夏綏銀宥節度使。

translations.literal: For his merit he was concurrently made Censor-in-Chief and military commissioner of Xia-Sui-Yin-You.
translations.idiomatic: For these deeds he was made concurrent Censor-in-Chief and commissioner of Xia-Sui-Yin-You.

sentences.zh: 又徙靈鹽。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Ling-Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He was next transferred to Ling-Yan.

sentences.zh: 部有光祿渠，久廞廢，聽始復屯田以省轉餉，即引渠溉塞下地千頃，後賴其饒。

translations.literal: Within his circuit was the Guanglu Canal, long choked and abandoned; Ting first restored garrison farming to save transport costs, then drew the canal to irrigate a thousand qing of low land along the frontier—later generations relied on its abundance.
translations.idiomatic: His circuit held the Guanglu Canal, long silted shut; Li Ting revived garrison farms to cut transport costs, reopened the canal, and irrigated a thousand qing of borderland—later generations lived off that plenty.

sentences.zh: 進檢校工部尚書。

translations.literal: He was advanced to acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 穆宗初立，幽、鎮反，擇名臣節度太原者代裴度，使統兵北討。

translations.literal: When Muzong first took the throne, You and Zhen rebelled; they chose a renowned minister to command Taiyuan in Pei Du's place and sent him to marshal troops for the northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: At Muzong's accession, Youzhou and Zhenzhou rose in revolt; the court chose a famed minister to replace Pei Du at Taiyuan and lead the northern armies.

sentences.zh: 始聽為羽林時，有駿馬，帝在東宮，使左右諷取之，聽自以身宿衛，不敢獻。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Ting was in the Feathered Forest, he had a fine steed; the emperor, then heir apparent, had his attendants hint that he should yield it—Ting, bound by his own duty as palace guard, did not dare present it.
translations.idiomatic: Years before, while Li Ting served in the Feathered Forest, he owned a splendid horse; the crown prince sent attendants to hint he should surrender it, but Ting, bound to guard duty, would not part with it.

sentences.zh: 於是帝曰：「李聽往在軍中，不與朕馬，是必可任。」

translations.literal: Thereupon the emperor said: "Li Ting, when he was in the army, would not give me his horse—he is surely fit for trust."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then said, "Li Ting once refused me his horse in camp—such a man can surely be trusted."

sentences.zh: 乃授檢校兵部尚書，充河東節度使。

translations.literal: He was thereupon appointed acting Minister of War and made military commissioner of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He was made acting Minister of War and military commissioner of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 敬宗嗣位，改義成軍。

translations.literal: When Jingzong succeeded, he was transferred to the Yicheng Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingzong succeeded, Li Ting was shifted to command Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 太和初，討李同捷，而魏博將丌志沼反，擊其帥史憲誠，詔聽出援，擊殺志沼。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe they campaigned against Li Tongjie; the Weibo general Qi Zhizhao rebelled and attacked his commander Shi Xiancheng—an edict ordered Ting to march out in relief, and he struck and killed Zhizhao.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taihe, as the court moved against Li Tongjie, Weibo general Qi Zhizhao rebelled and attacked his commander Shi Xiancheng; Li Ting was ordered to relieve him and slew Zhizhao in battle.

sentences.zh: 以功封涼國公，拜一子五品官。

translations.literal: For his merit he was enfeoffed Duke of Liang and one son was granted a fifth-rank office.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was enfeoffed Duke of Liang, and one son received a fifth-rank post.

sentences.zh: 王廷湊之亂，詔聽悉兵屯貝州，史憲誠懼聽因取道襲之，衷甲候諸郊。

translations.literal: During Wang Tingcou's rebellion, an edict ordered Ting to mass all his troops at Bei Prefecture; Shi Xiancheng feared Ting would seize the road and strike him, and wore armor waiting at every outskirts.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Tingcou rebelled, Li Ting was ordered to concentrate his forces at Bei; Shi Xiancheng, fearing a flanking strike, posted armored pickets along every approach.

sentences.zh: 聽敕士櫜兵野次，魏人乃安。

translations.literal: Ting ordered his men to sheath their weapons and camp in the open; the men of Weibo then grew calm.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ting ordered his men to camp with arms sheathed, and the Weibo troops were reassured.

sentences.zh: 憲誠既請朝，魏人怨，詔聽兼帥魏博。

translations.literal: After Xiancheng had requested an audience at court, the people of Weibo resented him; an edict made Ting concurrently commander of Weibo.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiancheng sought leave to attend court, Weibo turned against him, and Li Ting was ordered to take Weibo as well.

sentences.zh: 聽遷延不即赴，魏遂亂，殺憲誠，共推大將何進滔乘城拒守。

translations.literal: Ting delayed and did not go at once; Weibo thereupon mutinied, killed Xiancheng, and together raised the great general He Jintao to seize the walls and hold out.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ting lingered and would not enter at once; Weibo mutinied, slew Xiancheng, and set the great general He Jintao on the walls to resist.

sentences.zh: 聽不得入，乃屯館陶。

translations.literal: Ting could not enter and therefore encamped at Guantao.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to enter the city, Li Ting encamped at Guantao.

sentences.zh: 又不設備，魏人襲之，師驚潰，死失殆半，輜械盡棄之，聽晝夜馳以免。

translations.literal: Again he made no preparations; the men of Weibo raided him—the army broke in panic, deaths and losses reaching nearly half, baggage and weapons all abandoned; Ting galloped day and night to escape.
translations.idiomatic: He took no precautions; Weibo struck by night, the army broke in panic, nearly half were killed or scattered, and all baggage was abandoned—Li Ting rode day and night to save himself.

sentences.zh: 於是御史中丞溫造等劾奏魏州亂，憲誠死，職繇於聽，請論如法。

translations.literal: Thereupon Vice Censor-in-Chief Wen Zao and others memorialized impeaching him: the Wei Prefecture turmoil, Xiancheng's death—the office lay at Ting's door; they asked that he be judged according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Censor-in-Chief Wen Zao and others impeached him, blaming Li Ting for the Wei mutiny and Xiancheng's death and demanding punishment under law.

sentences.zh: 天子不罪也，罷為太子少師。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven did not punish him and dismissed him to heir-apparent Junior Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not punish him but relieved him to heir-apparent Junior Mentor.

sentences.zh: 聽素以賂遺得權幸心，故多為助力。

translations.literal: Ting had long won the hearts of the powerful through gifts and bribes, and so many lent him their aid.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ting had long bought favor with gifts among the powerful, and many now spoke for him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜邠甯節度使。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed military commissioner of Binning.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made military commissioner of Binning.

sentences.zh: 邠署相傳不利治垣舍，前刺史視其壞，莫敢葺。

translations.literal: At Bin headquarters it was handed down that repairing walls and quarters brought ill fortune; former prefects, seeing them ruined, none dared restore them.
translations.idiomatic: Binning headquarters had a legend that repairing the walls brought misfortune; prefect after prefect had let them crumble and none dared mend them.

sentences.zh: 聽曰：「將出鑿凶門，何避治署邪？」

translations.literal: Ting said: "When a general goes forth he breaks open the Gate of Ill Omen—why shrink from repairing the government offices?"
translations.idiomatic: Li Ting said, "A general marches out through the Gate of Ill Omen—why fear to repair the headquarters?"

sentences.zh: 亟使完新之，卒無異。

translations.literal: He promptly had them fully restored anew, and in the end nothing untoward occurred.
translations.idiomatic: He had them rebuilt at once, and no ill befell him.

sentences.zh: 改帥武寧軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to command the Wuning Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to command Wuning.

sentences.zh: 有故奴為徐將，不喜聽來，乃先殺親吏之使徐者以沮聽。

translations.literal: A former bondservant of his had become a Xu general and did not welcome Ting's arrival; he first killed the intimate clerk sent ahead to Xu in order to deter Ting.
translations.idiomatic: A former bondsman of his had become a Xu general and resented Li Ting's coming; he murdered the advance clerk sent to Xu to frighten him off.

sentences.zh: 聽果懼，以疾解，授太子少保。

translations.literal: Ting was indeed afraid and resigned on grounds of illness, receiving appointment as heir-apparent Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ting took fright, pleaded illness, and was made heir-apparent Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，節度鳳翔，又徙陳許。

translations.literal: After a year he was made military commissioner of Fengxiang, then transferred again to Chen-Xu.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he took Fengxiang, then was shifted to Chen-Xu.

sentences.zh: 鄭注摭其過，詔以太子太保分司東都。

translations.literal: Zheng Zhu gathered his faults; an edict made him heir-apparent Grand Preceptor with honorary duty at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zhu collected charges against him, and an edict sent him to the Eastern Capital as honorary heir-apparent Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 開成初，為河中晉絳慈隰節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaicheng he became military commissioner of Hezhong-Jin-Jiang-Ci-Long.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Kaicheng he was made commissioner of Hezhong-Jin-Jiang-Ci-Long.

sentences.zh: 文宗歎曰：「付之兵不疑，退處散地不怨，惟聽為可。」

translations.literal: Wenzong sighed and said: "Entrust him with troops and he is not doubted; set him aside in an idle post and he does not resent it—only Ting can do this."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong sighed and said, "Give him an army and he serves without suspicion; set him aside and he bears no grudge—only Li Ting can do that."

sentences.zh: 四年，以疾求還，復拜太子太保。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he asked to return on grounds of illness and was again appointed heir-apparent Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he asked leave for illness and was again made heir-apparent Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十一，贈司徒。

translations.literal: He died at sixty-one; posthumously he was given the office of Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-one and was posthumously made Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 聽治官苛細，急揫斂，頗極所欲，盛飾車馬服玩。

translations.literal: Ting governed with harsh minuteness, urgently squeezing revenue, going quite to the limit of his desires, and lavishly adorning carriages, horses, and curios.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ting governed with petty severity, squeezed revenue hard, indulged his every whim, and kept carriages, horses, and finery in splendid array.

sentences.zh: 或誡之，聽曰：「家聲在人，若示衰薄，恐不見忠功之效，吾欲誇而勸之也。」

translations.literal: Someone admonished him; Ting said: "A family's reputation rests on its people—if one shows decline and poverty, I fear the effect of loyal merit will not be seen; I wish to display splendor and thereby encourage it."
translations.idiomatic: When someone warned him, Li Ting said, "A house's standing rests on its men—show poverty and no one will see what loyalty can earn; I mean to display success and urge others toward it."

sentences.zh: 好方書，擇其驗者，題於帷帟牆屋皆滿。

translations.literal: He loved prescription books; those he found verified he copied, and curtains, screens, and walls were all filled with them.
translations.idiomatic: He loved medical texts, copied every recipe that had proved true, and covered curtains, screens, and walls with them.

sentences.zh: 聽子 琢

translations.literal: Ting's son: Zhuo
translations.idiomatic: Li Ting's son: Li Zhuo

sentences.zh: 聽子琢，以家閥擢累義昌、平盧、鎮海三節度使，無顯功，不為士大夫稱道。

translations.literal: Ting's son Zhuo, by family eminence promoted in succession to the three posts of military commissioner of Yichang, Pinglu, and Zhenhai, had no marked achievement and was not praised by scholar-officials.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhuo, Li Ting's son, rose by pedigree alone through three commands—Yichang, Pinglu, and Zhenhai—without notable merit and won no praise from the literati.

sentences.zh: 數免復遷。

translations.literal: Repeatedly dismissed, repeatedly transferred again.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed again and again, yet always reappointed.

sentences.zh: 廣明時，沙陀數盜邊，於是琢為宿將，拜檢校尚書右僕射，蔚朔等州招討、都統、行營節度使。

translations.literal: In the Guangming era the Shatuo repeatedly raided the frontier; Zhuo was then a veteran commander and was appointed acting Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, pacification commissioner, supreme commander, and field headquarters military commissioner of Wei, Shuo, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangming, as Shatuo raids multiplied, Li Zhuo was treated as a veteran and made acting Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, with overall command of the Wei-Shuo pacification army.

sentences.zh: 徙河陽三城，坐逗撓，下遷刺史，卒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Heyang Three Garrisons; for dilatory campaigning he was demoted to prefect and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was shifted to the Heyang Three Garrisons, demoted to prefect for slack campaigning, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 甥 王佖

translations.literal: Nephew: Wang Tian
translations.idiomatic: Nephew: Wang Tian

sentences.zh: 王佖者，晟之甥，武敢，閑騎射。

translations.literal: Wang Tian was Sheng's nephew—bold in war, skilled in horsemanship and archery.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tian, Li Sheng's nephew, was bold in battle and expert in horsemanship and archery.

sentences.zh: 晟在師，佖無不從。

translations.literal: Whenever Sheng was on campaign, Tian followed in everything.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Li Sheng marched, Wang Tian followed.

sentences.zh: 攻硃泚於光泰門，賊方銳，佖與李演鏖戰蹀血，賊數北，諸軍乘之，遂大振。

translations.literal: Attacking Zhu Ci at Guangtai Gate, the rebels were at their sharpest; Tian and Li Yan fought a bloody pitched battle, the rebels repeatedly retreated north, the various armies pressed the advantage, and the tide turned greatly.
translations.idiomatic: At Guangtai Gate, as Zhu Ci's men were at their fiercest, Wang Tian and Li Yan fought until the ground ran with blood; the rebels broke again and again, the allied armies pressed home, and the day was won.

sentences.zh: 以功擢神策將。

translations.literal: For his merit he was promoted to general of the Divine Strategy Army.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was promoted to general of the Divine Strategy Army.

sentences.zh: 擊吐蕃有功。

translations.literal: Striking the Tibetans he had achievement.
translations.idiomatic: He won distinction fighting the Tibetans.

sentences.zh: 晟視佖與子姓等，其給與過之。

translations.literal: Sheng regarded Tian as equal to his own sons by clan, and his gifts to him exceeded theirs.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng treated Wang Tian as one of his own sons and lavished on him more than on any of them.

sentences.zh: 晟兵罷，佖亦不見用，召為左衛上將軍。

translations.literal: When Sheng's armies were disbanded, Tian likewise was not employed and was summoned as Senior General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Sheng's armies were stood down, Wang Tian too fell from favor and was recalled as senior general of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 元和中，拜朔方、靈鹽節度使。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era he was appointed military commissioner of Shuofang and Ling-Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe he was made military commissioner of Shuofang and Ling-Yan.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃欲作烏蘭橋以過師，積材河曲，朔方府常遣兵發其木，委於河，故莫能成。

translations.literal: The Tibetans wished to build the Wulan Bridge to cross the army's path; they piled timber along the river bend—the Shuofang headquarters often sent troops to tear up the wood and cast it into the river, and so they could not complete it.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans tried to build the Wulan Bridge to cut the army's line; they stacked timber along the bend, but Shuofang repeatedly sent men to tear it up and throw it in the river, so the bridge never stood.

sentences.zh: 及佖至，虜知其寡謀，乃厚賂之而亟遂功，築月城以守。

translations.literal: When Tian arrived, the barbarians knew he lacked counsel; they richly bribed him and quickly finished the work, building a moon fort to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Tian arrived, the Tibetans saw he was no strategist; they bribed him heavily, finished the bridge at once, and raised a crescent fort to guard it.

sentences.zh: 自是虜歲入為寇，朔方乘障不暇，人以咎佖。

translations.literal: From then on the barbarians yearly entered as raiders; Shuofang manned the barriers without respite, and men blamed Tian.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the Tibetans raided every year; Shuofang's garrisons never rested, and blame fell on Wang Tian.

sentences.zh: 在鎮檢下亡術，猜忌多殺人。

translations.literal: While in command he was harsh in inspecting subordinates and lacked sound methods; suspicious, he killed many.
translations.idiomatic: In command he bullied his subordinates without sound policy, grew suspicious, and put many to death.

sentences.zh: 召還為右衛將軍。

translations.literal: He was recalled and made general of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as general of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 故事，將相除徙，皆內出制，故號「白麻」；

translations.literal: By precedent, the appointment and transfer of generals and chancellors all issued as edicts from within the palace, and so they were called "white hemp";
translations.idiomatic: By custom, appointments and dismissals of generals and chancellors came as edicts from within the palace—hence the name "white hemp";

sentences.zh: 至佖，以責罷，遂中書進制。

translations.literal: as for Tian, he was dismissed under censure, and the edict was therefore submitted through the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: but Wang Tian's dismissal for fault went through the Secretariat instead.

sentences.zh: 久之，卒。

translations.literal: After a long while he died.
translations.idiomatic: In time he died.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：晟之屯東渭橋也，硃泚盜京師，李懷光反咸陽，河北三叛相王，李納猘河南，李希烈訌鄭、汳。

translations.literal: The encomium says: When Sheng encamped at East Wei Bridge, Zhu Ci stole the capital, Li Huai'guang rebelled at Xianyang, the three rebels of Hebei each styled themselves king, Li Na ravaged Henan, and Li Xilie rebelled in Zheng and Bian.
translations.idiomatic: The chroniclers write: When Li Sheng held East Wei Bridge, Zhu Ci seized the capital, Li Huai'guang rebelled at Xianyang, the three Hebei warlords crowned one another kings, Li Na ravaged Henan, and Li Xilie rose in Zheng and Bian.

sentences.zh: 晟無積貲輸糧，提孤軍抗群賊，身佩安危而氣不少衰者，徒以忠誼感人，故豪英樂為之死耳。

translations.literal: Sheng had no stored wealth to forward grain; he led a lone army against a host of rebels, bearing the realm's safety on his person yet his spirit did not wane in the least—this was solely because loyalty and righteousness moved men's hearts, and so heroes gladly died for him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng had no hoarded stores to feed his men, yet led a lone army against a host of rebels, bearing the empire's fate on his shoulders without faltering—solely because loyalty and righteousness won men's hearts, and heroes gladly died for him.

sentences.zh: 至師入長安而人不知，雖三王之佐，無進其能，可謂仁義將矣！

translations.literal: When his army entered Chang'an and the people did not know it—even the assistants of the Three Kings could not match his ability; he may be called a general of benevolence and righteousness!
translations.idiomatic: His army entered Chang'an before the people knew he had won—assistants to the sage kings of antiquity could not have surpassed him; he was truly a general of benevolence and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，功能存社祏，不能見信於庸主，卒奪其兵，哀哉！

translations.literal: Alas! His merit could preserve the altars of state, yet he could not win trust from a mediocre sovereign and in the end was stripped of his army—how lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: Alas—a man whose merit saved the altars of state could not win a mediocre emperor's trust and was stripped of his army at last. How bitter!

sentences.zh: 雖然，功蓋天下者，惟退禍可以免。

translations.literal: Even so, for one whose achievement covers all under Heaven, only withdrawal can escape calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet for one whose deeds overshadow the realm, only withdrawal can escape ruin.

sentences.zh: 四子世似其勞，是宜有後哉。

translations.literal: His four sons for generations resembled his toil—surely descendants were fitting!
translations.idiomatic: His four sons bore his burden down the generations—surely such a house deserved posterity.
